## C17-S1/S2/S3: joint clone model, transplant split test, cortical instruction vs selection (pre-registered 2026-11-18; Bence: "1" = pre-register S1-S3)
- **Serves: C17-S0** item (3) (pre-register S1 joint fit, S2 leave-one-system-out, S3 sealed look). Scripts: `c17s1_joint.py` (S1, train only), `c17s2_loso.py` (S2, train only), `c17s3_look.py` (S3, oracle). FOCUS moves to C17-S1 only after `lit/novelty/C17-S1.md`.
- **S1 (train only): joint hierarchical fit of `core_model.py`.** Systems with an existing configuration: LARRY cytokine wells (E53), SIS (E52), Raj gastruloids (C3-S1); plus train rows of rf2020_clone and cortical_clone. Shared hyperpriors on memory (rho per division), instruction (tau) and selection (gamma) scales; per-system nuisance (sampling depth, growth). Selection by train cross-validation (H12, selection/c17s1.json). Two embedded tests on train, exploratory:
  - **T-split (rf2020_clone train):** within-clone lineage-bias agreement across the two recipients a clone was split into. Statistic: Spearman rho of per-recipient lineage-bias score (fraction of a clone's Kit+ compartment cells in each projected lineage, first principal axis fitted on train), across clones shared with >= 3 cells in each recipient. Null: clones shuffled within recipient and sample set (1,000 shuffles). Separated from potency: partial rho given log clone size in each recipient.
  - **T-cortical (cortical_clone train):** per guide target vs non-targeting, decompose the shift in clonal fate bias into instruction (fate distribution within surviving clones of matched size) and selection (clone-size by fate-class), the chapter 1-2 decomposition with clone as unit and guide as clone-level treatment.
- **S2 (train only): leave-one-system-out.** Freeze shared hyperparameters fitted on all other systems; predict the held-out system's clone statistics (sister/split agreement, clone-size distribution summary, fate-coupling). Score: log predictive density vs (a) per-system fit, (b) no-sharing baseline. Pass = beats (b) on >= 3 of 5 systems, and on rf2020_clone (not seen in the fit).
- **S3 (sealed, one partition each, A first):** frozen S1/S2 code and predictions committed before the look (H6). Primary sealed tests:
  1. T-split on rf2020_clone:A, one-sided rho > 0.
  2. T-cortical instruction component, per guide target vs non-targeting, on cortical_clone:A.
- **Pre-flight:**
  1. Unit: clone (both sets). T-split: clone shared across recipients; recipients are not contrasted, so the H22 per-arm rule applies only to T-cortical: arms = guide target (5) vs non-targeting, clone-level assignment; >= 3 donor batches per arm checked on train before S1 statistics, else that guide drops.
  2. Readout: T-split, per-recipient lineage-bias score from projected lineage labels (GSE134242 fate files, train rows via train_only); T-cortical, clonal cluster label and n_cells.
  3. Used data first: LARRY, SIS, Raj (used) carry the joint fit; new sets enter through train_only.
  4. Power (power.py, sealed counts from c17s0c_seal.json): shared clones per partition A 30 / B 31 / C 31, train 60.
     - T-split: rho_power n=30: rho 0.3 -> 0.36, 0.4 -> 0.60, **0.5 -> 0.81**, 0.6 -> 0.95. Pooled A+B (n=61): rho 0.4 -> 0.90.
     - T-cortical (clones in A, sd-scaled effect d): ARX vs NT (651 vs 283): d 0.2 -> 0.80; smallest arm NR2E1 vs NT (105 vs 283): d 0.3 -> 0.75.

  5. Exposure: S0b structure counts, S0c partition counts, claims-level reads of the source papers (accepted). The 2020 paper claims potency is intrinsic across split recipients; the 2026 paper claims lineage bias is extrinsic. Our prediction, stated now: T-split rho > 0 (intrinsic component of lineage bias survives the split), partial rho given size > 0.

Readout gate (H21), checked on train before any test statistic: outcome distribution of lineage-bias scores shown; >= 30 units per side (T-split train 60 shared clones; T-cortical >= 208 clones per arm in train); statistic differs between intrinsic and shuffled models on synthetic data; carrying units = shared clones (mostly sample set 5).

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 1 (2026-11-18; Bence: "go 2 and 3")
- **Primary sealed test: T-cortical instruction component** (per guide target vs non-targeting, clone = unit). **T-split becomes secondary** (exploratory unless it passes the power gate). Reason: T-split has about 30 shared clones per partition, most of them in one sample set, and it is partly published (2020: clone-expansion agreement across recipients). The direct lineage-bias version is not found.
- T-split must beat the published expansion agreement: the primary T-split statistic is the **partial** rho of lineage bias given log clone size in each recipient (raw rho reported but not tested).
- Exposure added: one pooled 2020 result sentence on across-recipient clone-expansion correlation (lit/novelty/C17-S0.md). It is not used as an effect prior.
- H22 re-check: unchanged. Cortical arms are guide targets with clone-level assignment, and >= 3 donor batches per arm is checked on train. T-split is not a between-condition contrast.

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 2: T-split rewritten to test only the novel claim (2026-11-18; Bence: "rewrite the split test to claim what is novel")
- **Published (not claimed by us):** a clone's expansion and frequency agree across the two recipients it was split into (2020 paper; earlier report it cites).
- **Novel claim under test (T-split'):** *a clone's lineage bias is partly intrinsic.* Two halves of the same HSC clone, in two different hosts, make the same mix of lineages, beyond what clone size or potency predicts. This adjudicates directly between "potency intrinsic" (2020) and "lineage bias extrinsic" (2026), which neither paper tested.
- **Units:** clones shared across the two recipients, with >= 3 Kit+ compartment (progenitor/mature) cells in each recipient. Sample sets S1, S2, S4, S5; S3 has one recipient and is excluded.
- **Readout:** per clone per recipient, the lineage composition of its Kit+ cells (Mk, Ery, GM/Ba, preDC, preB from the projected labels). This is a closed composition, so we use the centred log-ratio with a 0.5 pseudocount.
- **Primary statistic: size-matched intrinsic share (ICC).** Between-clone variance of the lineage composition across the two recipients over total variance (one-way random-effects ICC on the first train-fitted CLR axis). Null: within each sample set, each clone's recipient-2 composition is swapped with that of another clone in the same size bin (quintiles of log total cells, summed over both recipients) and the same recipient. 2,000 swaps. Size cannot create agreement under this null, so a positive ICC beyond it is lineage-bias agreement not explained by size. One-sided, alpha 0.025.
- **Secondary (descriptive, not tested):** (a) Aitchison distance between a clone's two halves vs size-matched non-sister pairs; (b) the same ICC within HSC-compartment cells (state agreement); (c) per-lineage agreement (does Mk bias, which the 2020 paper ties to low output, carry the intrinsic share?); (d) host effect: the shift of the recipient mean composition, the extrinsic component.
- **Predictions, stated now:** intrinsic-only model, ICC near the published expansion agreement; extrinsic-only (2026), ICC ~ 0 after size matching, with a host shift in (d). Our prediction: ICC > 0, smaller than expansion agreement, with a nonzero host shift. Lineage bias is then part intrinsic and part extrinsic, and both papers are partly right.
- **Claim wording if the test passes on A, then replicates on B (frozen):** "In split-clone transplants, an HSC clone's lineage bias agrees between hosts beyond clone size (intrinsic share X, 95% CI); the rest is host-dependent." On A alone the result is reported as "confirmed once"; the word "claim" needs A and B.
- **Power (power.py; ICC treated as a correlation, two halves per clone):** 30 shared clones per partition (A 30 / B 31 / C 31). Clones with < 3 Kit+ cells per recipient drop, so the count is checked on train before any statistic (if train has < 30, the test stays exploratory). rho_power n=30: ICC 0.5 -> 0.81, 0.57 -> 0.92 (0.9 reached at about 0.55). The look gate is 0.9 at half the train estimate; otherwise a pooled A+B look (n 61; ICC 0.4 -> 0.90) needs Bence's OK, and C stays as reserve.
- **Self-challenge, built in:** sample set 5 carries about 72% of shared clones, so ICC is reported per sample set and the null is within sample set. Shared clones are selected for engrafting twice (potent clones); the claim is restricted to "engrafting clones". Projection labels come from the authors' classifier, shared across recipients, which cannot by itself create clone-specific agreement under the clone-swap null.
- **Synthetic smoke tests before the real run:** (1) planted intrinsic bias plus host shift, ICC recovered; (2) size-only model (bias a function of size), ICC ~ 0 under the size-matched null; (3) host-only model, ICC ~ 0.
- H22: not a between-condition contrast, so unchanged. Exposure: unchanged since amendment 1.

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 3: published expansion agreement kept as the anchor of the novel claim (2026-11-18; Bence: "we can even leave in the not novel stuff if it helps prove our novel claim if those in pair are stronger")
- **Paired design:** on the same clones, partition and null, we measure (i) the published quantity, the agreement of clone expansion across the two hosts (ICC of log cells per recipient), and (ii) the novel quantity, the size-matched agreement of lineage bias (amendment 2).
- **Roles:**
  1. **Positive control / adequacy gate:** (i) must replicate on train (one-sided, alpha 0.025) before any T-split' look. If the assay cannot recover the published agreement on our parse of the data, a null result for (ii) is uninterpretable, and T-split' stops. (Exposure: the pooled published value is known, so this is a replication of a known result, not a discovery.)
  2. **Headline novel quantity: ratio R = ICC_bias / ICC_expansion** (how heritable lineage bias is, relative to potency, in the same clones), with a 95% CI by clone bootstrap. The 2026 extrinsic view predicts R ~ 0; a fully intrinsic view predicts R ~ 1; our prediction is 0 < R < 1.
  3. **Bivariate clone model (S1, core_model.py):** per clone, latent potency and latent bias, each with clone and host components. It estimates the intrinsic share of each and their clone-level correlation (is the bias that carries over the low-output Mk bias tied to potency?). Model fit is descriptive; the tested statistic stays (ii).
- **What carries the claim:** the sealed test remains (ii) alone: size-matched ICC_bias > 0 on A, replicated on B. A combined or summed statistic is **not** used for significance, because a pass could then come from the published part alone. R and the bivariate fit are reported with CIs as support. The pairing strengthens interpretation (same clones, same parse, control passed, effect scaled to a published anchor); it does not add power to (ii) after size matching, and we say so.
- **Claim wording if (ii) passes on A and B:** "In split-clone transplants, an HSC clone's lineage bias agrees between hosts beyond clone size, at about R of the agreement of its expansion (95% CI); the rest is host-dependent."
- H22 unchanged; exposure unchanged since amendment 1. Amendment count within this step: 3 (H18 retro before a 5th).

### C17-S1 run 1 result (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44504514112)
- The run was marked failed only because the JSON writer could not serialise numpy booleans in the pass dict. All statistics were written before that; the pass rules are evaluated here from the written values. Writer fixed (default=item).

The size-binned clone-swap null separates intrinsic bias from size and host on synthetic data. - **Smoke, T-cortical:** null ~0 (PASS). Pure instruction +0.15 at both floors (PASS). **Pure selection, floor 1:** clone-count instruction +0.011 (sd 0.044; PASS). **Pure selection, floor 3: +0.055 (sd 0.045): FAIL.** Once small clones drop below detection, faster growth of one fate class leaks into the clone-count fate fraction. The size-matched variant leaks less (+0.032) but still FAILS. Neither estimator is selection-proof under a detection floor.
- **Train checks (counts only):**
  - rf2020_clone: Kit+ libraries exist in all five sample sets. Shared train clones with >= 3 Kit+ cells in each recipient: **36** (S5 30, S4 4, S1 2). The gate >= 30 PASSES, but S5 carries 83%.

- **Consequence:** T-cortical cannot go to the joint fit until an instruction estimator passes the floor-3 smoke. This needs amendment 4 (candidates: a truncated-count model of detection, fitted jointly with growth by fate; or restricting to clones far above the floor). T-split' proceeds; with 36 train clones, its train estimate will be noisy (simulated power ~0.6 at the planted effect).

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 4: detection-aware cortical estimator (2026-11-19; Bence: "Yes, amendment 4")
- Reason: run 1 smoke. Both clone-count and size-matched instruction leak under pure selection once clones below a detection floor are lost (floor 3: +0.055 and +0.032).
- **New T-cortical estimator:** per arm (guide target, NT) and fate class, fit a negative binomial to clone sizes **truncated below at the detection floor** (MLE). Detected clones are scaled by 1 / P(detect) to recover the clone count at birth. **Instruction** = corrected fate fraction (guide - NT); **selection** = difference in log fitted mean size between fate classes (guide - NT). On real data: fate class = `Clonal cluster` (multi-class). The instruction statistic per guide is the total-variation distance between corrected fate distributions (guide vs NT), with a null that permutes guide labels within donor batch (1,000). Floor = the observed train minimum `n_cells` (structure count from the checks stage).
- **Smoke pass rules (fixed now), floors 1, 3 and 5, 200 reps:** under pure selection, |corrected instruction| < 0.5 sd; under pure instruction, corrected instruction > 0.1; under pure selection, corrected selection > 0.4 (planted log 2 = 0.69). If any rule fails, T-cortical stays exploratory (no sealed look), and S1 proceeds with T-split' and the joint fit.
- Assumption stated: clone size follows a negative binomial within (arm, fate class). Misfit is checked on train by a posterior-predictive size distribution before any test (adequacy gate).
- H22 unchanged (clone-level assignment, >= 11 donor batches per arm). Exposure unchanged. **This is the 4th amendment in this step; a 5th requires a retro first (H18).**

### C17-S1 run 2 result (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44507674489; synthetic + train counts)
- The sweep reports "fail" on its single line, but both result files are complete, with the pass dict written. The cause of the non-zero exit is not yet found. It is noted and will be fixed before the next run.
- **T-split' smoke:** all pass again (unchanged code).
- **Detection-aware cortical estimator (amendment 4):** no leak at any floor. Under pure selection, corrected instruction is -0.003 / -0.010 / -0.014 at floors 1 / 3 / 5 (all within 0.5 sd: PASS).
  - Instruction is detected at floors 1 and 3 (+0.152, +0.138) but **not at floor 5 (+0.086 < 0.1): FAIL** by the fixed all-floors rule.
  - Variance grows with the floor: instruction sd 0.045 / 0.09-0.13 / 0.24-0.32.
  - The selection estimate is biased under the null at floors 3 and 5 (-0.31, -0.86). Selection detection passes formally but is not trustworthy above floor 1.
- **Real train detection floor:** minimum n_cells = 3 (train clones with 3 / 4 / 5 cells: 1,501 / 875 / 527), so the real data sit in the floor-3 regime, where instruction passes but with about 2-3x the noise.
- **Decision by the fixed rule:** a pass rule failed (floor 5), so **T-cortical is exploratory (no sealed look)**. Floor 5 is not the real data's regime. Re-scoping the rule to the observed floor would be a 5th amendment and needs a retro first (H18); that is Bence's call. S1 proceeds with T-split', the expansion control and the joint fit.

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 5: cortical pass rules re-scoped to the observed regime (2026-11-19; Bence: "1"; retro RETRO_2026-11-19.md first, H18)
- Serves: C17-S1. Script `c17s1_joint.py --stage smoke`.
- The detection floor is the observed train minimum: **3 cells** (run 2 counts). Floor 5 is dropped from the rules (reported, not gated).
- Pass rules (fixed before the run): under pure selection, |corrected instruction| < 0.5 sd at floors 1 and 3; under pure instruction, corrected instruction > 0.1 at floors 1 and 3. **New: power at the real train arm sizes and floor 3** (NT 564 vs smallest arm 208, and vs largest 1,302; planted shift 0.15; one-sided alpha 0.025 against the simulated null). Power >= 0.8 for both arm sizes, and false-positive rate under pure selection <= 0.06.
- Selection component: descriptive only (biased under the null above floor 1, run 2); never tested.
- If the rules pass, T-cortical is restored as the primary sealed test. If not, it stays exploratory, with no further amendment in this step.
- Practice: lines of 2026-11-19 applied (regime measured first; 1-rep local writer run done).
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1_smoke5.txt); retro gap map (sweeps/retro_c17s1_gap.txt).

### C17-S1/S2/S3 amendment 6: our own lineage labels for the split test (2026-11-19; Bence: "go" to amendment 6; retro RETRO_2026-11-19.md already done, H18)
- Serves: C17-S1. Script `c17s1_joint.py --stage train` (Actions; train rows only via partitions.train_only, filtered before any scoring).
- **Reason:** published per-cell lineage labels exist only for Sample2 (as numeric cluster IDs, no names) and Sample3. Sample5, Sample4 and Sample1, which hold all 36 shared train clones (30 / 4 / 2; Sample2 has none in train), have normalised expression only (genes x cells CSV). Format check: counts only (H9).
- **Labels (fixed now, before any expression read):** marker sets (mouse): Mk Pf4, Itga2b, Gp9, Vwf; Ery Klf1, Car1, Gata1, Hba-a1; GM Mpo, Elane, Ctsg, Prtn3; Ba/Mast Prss34, Cpa3, Mcpt8; preDC Irf8, Siglech, Cd74; preB Vpreb1, Dntt, Ebf1, Igll1. Score = mean log1p(normalised counts) over a lineage's markers, z-scored per lineage across train Kit+ cells. Label = argmax z if z_max >= 1.0, else unassigned (progenitor/HSC-like).
- **Validation gate (before any split statistic):** on Sample2 train cells, each authors' cluster ID is mapped to the lineage that most of its cells receive. Gate: cell-weighted purity >= 0.8 (cells in a cluster carrying that cluster's majority label, unassigned counted as its own label). Fail = the split test stops; no relabelling.
- **Order of statistics on train:**
  1. Readout gate (H21): distribution of per-clone-recipient lineage composition and bias score (quantiles), units counted.
  2. Expansion control: ICC of log total barcoded cells per recipient across shared clones; clone-swap null within sample set (1,000). It must pass at one-sided alpha 0.025, or the split test stops.
  3. T-split': bias = first principal axis of CLR (counts + 0.5) of assigned Kit+ lineage counts per clone-recipient, fitted on train. Size-adjusted, size-binned clone-swap ICC (smoke-tested code). Units: shared clones with >= 3 Kit+ cells per recipient.
  4. R = ICC_bias / ICC_expansion, with a 95% CI from a 1,000-draw clone bootstrap.
  5. Look gate for A computed from the half-shrunk train ICC (power.rho_power, n = 30, gate 0.9).
- Exposure: unchanged. Train only; A/B/C untouched. Cluster IDs carry no lineage names; their purity is a structural check of our labels.
- Practice: 1-rep local writer check on synthetic input before dispatch; regime measured (labels exist for S2 only), then rules fixed.
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1_train.txt).

## C17-S1R: the general model is built system by system (pre-registered 2026-11-19; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C17-S1.** Reason (inventory 2026-11-19, no statistic): only LARRY, SIS and the gastruloids carry fitted fate parameters. A cross-system law has the system as its unit, so 3 systems give no power. C5-S2 already showed that one memory law fails across committed blood and pluripotent clones, so any law needs a cell-class term, and H22 requires >= 3 systems per class. The joint fit of the original S1 is replaced by:
  1. **Parameter table** (`c17s1_params.py`): one row per system and parameter (memory per division, memory per event, instruction, selection, growth noise), each with point, interval, identifiability flag and log source. Used estimates only; no data read.
  2. **Grow the systems** with the time-split configuration of `core_model.py`, starting with CellTag LSK. Each new system is fitted on train rows only and fills the table.
  3. **The law test is pre-registered only when the table has >= 3 systems per cell class with identified parameters**, with power from power.py using systems as units.
- Serves: C17-S1 parameter table, script c17s1_params.py.
- Pre-flight: (table step) unit = system x parameter; readout = none (compilation); used data only; power n/a; exposure none new; literature: per-system sources already read; readout gate n/a.
- Practice: values are copied from logged results with line references, and the table script asserts each source line exists in EXPERIMENT_LOG.md (smoke against transcription errors).
- Compute: local because it is a compilation of logged numbers (no data, no simulation).
- T-cortical (exploratory) and T-split' (stopped) remain as recorded; S2/S3 wait for the law test.

The neural class is worth fitting if >= 3 sets (cortical_clone included) are memory-capable; then the next step is download sizes, Bence's OK for any download over 2 GB, and sealing by clone before any statistic.

## C17-S1P: sister-subclade heritable share in the embryo lineage trees, TRAIN embryos only (pre-registered 2026-11-19; Bence: "1 go")
- Serves: C17-S1 (C17-S1R: grow the systems; the pluripotent-derived class has 1 system). Script c17s1p_trees.py (reuses c14s0_gate.load_obs / iter_train_trees, which filter to train embryos with partitions.train_only before any other column, and sis_data.heritable_share / synthetic unchanged), on Actions with `--petracer`.
- Estimand: the B38 heritable share used for SIS and CellTag LSK, with the two children of a tree node as the two sister arms. H = (D_rand - D_sis) / (D_rand - D_noise) on per-subclade counts over the obs `lineage` categories; random partners within the same embryo.
- Sister pairs: a node qualifies if its clade has <= 300 leaves (C14's MAX_CLADE) and its two largest children each hold >= 4 annotated train cells (C7-S2 primary arm size). Qualifying nodes are taken smallest first and a node is skipped if it shares leaves with one already taken, so pairs are disjoint (independent units).
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: a disjoint sister-subclade pair; clustered in embryos (7 train embryos; the CI resamples embryos, then pairs).
  2. Readout: lineage label counts per subclade (already used on train in C14).
  3. Used data first: train embryos only; A (spent) and B/C (sealed) are skipped by key before parsing.
  4. Power: not a test; an estimate for the parameter table. Gate below.
  5. Exposure: as C14 (train cells, trees, labels).
  6. Literature: PEtracer source read at claims level (C13); fate coupling between sister clades is the authors' own topic, so this value is a parameter, not a claim.
  7. Readout gate (H21): >= 30 disjoint pairs, else stop.
- Smoke (before the real estimate, same run): syn0 (both arms drawn from the embryo's population fractions) must give |H| < 0.15 and syn1 (both arms from the pair's pooled fractions) H > 0.85, on the real pair sizes; otherwise INVALID. Offline selftest of the pair picker on a toy tree.
  - **Amendment 1 (before any real data, 2026-11-19):** the offline baseline showed that one synthetic draw has sd 0.15-0.26 for syn0 (60-500 pairs) and that syn1 tops out near 0.88 at 4 cells per arm, so the single-draw rule above would fail by chance or by the estimator's ceiling. The rule is now the **mean over 20 draws**: |mean syn0| < 0.15 and mean syn1 > 0.80; both means and sds are reported. (Practice line: thresholds get a baseline before they are fixed.)
- Prediction: H between the gastruloid's per-passage retention (0.46) and blood (0.66-0.88); written before the run.
- Limits written now: sister subclades in an embryo share a neighbourhood, so H here is memory plus shared niche (an upper bound on intrinsic memory); in SIS and CellTag the arms were separated into wells. The table row will carry this caveat. Exploratory secondary: H by clade-size tertile (deeper splits vs shallow), no claim.
- Practice: offline selftest of the pair picker; synthetic smoke on real pair sizes inside the run; peak RAM as C14 (streamed trees, train obs only); 1-rep writer check offline.
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1p.txt, `--petracer`).

### C17-S1P result (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44581668936; `results_c17/c17s1p_trees.json`; 7 TRAIN embryos only, nothing sealed read)
- 11,057 disjoint sister-subclade pairs (gate >= 30 met), 14 lineage categories, median arm 8 and 5 labelled cells.
- Smoke on the real arm sizes (20 draws): syn0 mean 0.07 (sd 0.02), syn1 mean 0.99 (sd 0.001): **PASS**.
- **Pre-registered estimate: H 0.81 [0.53, 0.87]** (CI from resampling embryos). D_sis 0.22, D_rand 0.77, D_noise 0.09. The prediction (between 0.46 and 0.88) was met.
- Exploratory (no claim):
  - By clade size: H 0.84 (median 11 leaves), 0.81 (17), 0.78 (28). Larger, older clades agree slightly less, the direction of memory lost per division.
  - **Per embryo, H rises with stage:** E7.5 -0.01, E8.0 0.27 and 0.32, E8.5 0.63 and 0.59, E9.0 0.79, E9.5 0.89. E9.0-E9.5 hold 80% of the pairs, so the pooled 0.81 mostly reflects late embryos.
- Self-challenge:
  1. **Stage dominates.** Later sister subclades sit inside lineages that are already committed, so their shared label is commitment by descent as much as ongoing memory. The pooled value is not one stage-free parameter. The early embryos (E7.5-E8.0, H about 0-0.3, few pairs) are the closest to an uncommitted state.
  2. **Shared niche:** sisters in an embryo stay neighbours, so H includes a shared environment (upper bound on intrinsic memory); in SIS and CellTag the arms were separated into wells.
  3. Units: 7 embryos; the CI is wide.
  4. Published? Fate coupling of related clades is the source study's own topic (claims level); this is a parameter for our table, not a claim.
- **Table:** added as "PEtracer embryo trees (train)", class pluripotent-derived, heritable_share 0.81 [0.53, 0.87], identified, with the stage and niche caveats. The pluripotent class now has **2 systems** (gastruloids, embryo trees); blood 3. Any cross-class law must model stage (or use the early embryos), because this system's memory value moves with developmental time.

## C17-S1C: CRISPR brain barcoding set (GSE210139), S0 download of the barcode tables and structure check (pre-registered 2026-11-19; Bence: "go" = download the CRISPR brain set)
- Serves: C17-S1 (C17-S1R: grow the systems; the neural class has this one sure memory-capable set). Script c17s1c_crest.py, stage `struct`.
- Download (Bence's OK covers the whole 12.7 GB set; taken in stages, smallest first): now only the two single-cell barcode QC tables (2.7 MB each, `GSE210139_single_cell_CREST_barcode_qc*.rds.gz`) into `data/ext_crest/raw/`, read with `python -I` and the `rdata` package (R data parser; no R code is executed). The expression objects (Seurat, 1.3-2.7 GB each) come only if this gate passes.
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: clone (cells sharing a founder barcode); sister subclades are groups of a clone's cells that share a further edited allele.
  2. Readout (this stage): structure only (H9): column names, row count, per-cell sample/stage/region tags, cells per clone, distinct alleles per clone. No cell type, no expression, no fate column is tabulated (columns whose names suggest a cell type are listed by name only).
  3. Used data first: none of this set is used.
  4. Power: the gate below.
  5. Exposure: barcode tables only.
  6. Literature: source paper not read yet (H20 before any estimate; claims level).
  7. Readout gate: S1 needs >= 30 eligible train clones (H21).
- **Gate (fixed now):** an eligible clone has >= 8 barcoded cells and at least two allele-defined subclades with >= 4 cells each (the C17-S1P arm size). Pass if 0.4 x eligible >= 30 (>= 75 eligible clones) and the table has a column that links each cell to an expression object (cell barcode plus sample). Pass: seal by clone (balanced_split, strata = sample), commit the map, then download the matching expression object(s) and pre-register S1. Fail: stop; nothing else downloaded.
- Practice: offline selftest of the structure functions on a synthetic table before the real read; peak RAM trivial (5 MB).
- Compute: local, because it is a structure read of two 2.7 MB files (under 2 minutes; nothing statistical).
- **Schema (2026-11-19, `results_c17/c17s1c_schema.json`):** the file is a list of per-sample tables (E11, E15, a second E11 series and organoids, 3 replicates each, plus merged copies; the replicates are stacked). 58,740 cells; columns: cell barcode, `pattern.v1` and `pattern.v2` (edits per target site of two barcode arrays; v1 missing for about half the cells), a combined `pattern`, `sample`, and a cell-type column (41 types; **not read**). The barcode table carries the fate labels itself, so the expression objects may not be needed.
- **Amendment 1 (before the gate; column mapping only, no fate read):** clone = cells sharing one informative `pattern.v2` that occurs in one sample only (recurrent alleles, "no edit" and single deletions spanning every site are homoplasy or uninformative); subclades = distinct informative `pattern.v1` within the clone. These subclades are related groups inside a clone, not proven sisters (no tree is reconstructed); a tree-based definition needs the source methods (H20) before S1. The gate rule is unchanged and is reported pooled and per sample group (E11, E15, second E11 series, organoids), since the groups may be separate systems.

### C17-S1C S0 result: gate FAILS under amendment 1, stop (2026-11-19; local; `results_c17/c17s1c_gate.json`; structure only, cell types not read)
- Clones are plentiful: 46,709 cells carry an informative v2 pattern; 26,386 of them in v2 patterns seen in one sample only; **2,731 such clones, 835 with >= 8 cells** (21,313 cells). 981 v2 patterns recur across samples (20,323 cells) and are excluded as homoplasy.
- **Subclades are not:** v1 is present for 9,854 of those cells, but only **336** carry an informative v1 pattern; most v1 arrays show one deletion over every site (the array is wiped). Eligible clones (>= 8 cells, >= 2 v1 subclades of >= 4): **0** in every group. Stop by the rule; the expression objects are not downloaded.
- What would rescue it (not done; needs a decision and the H20 methods read): subclades from shared edits inside the v2 array (cells of one clade share an early edit and differ in later ones), i.e. a tree from edit sharing, as the source study likely does. That is amendment 2 and a new structure check, not a re-tuning of this gate.
- Downloads so far: two 2.7 MB barcode tables in data/ext_crest/raw (SHA256SUMS there); nothing else.

### C17-S1C amendment 2: the split clones of pandaCREST (2026-11-19; Bence: "go" = rescue option 1; written before the gate count)
- H20 reading: the source paper (Nat Methods 2023, doi 10.1038/s41592-023-01947-3) is closed access; no free full text in Europe PMC. Read: PubMed abstract and the GEO summary/design (claims level). The design they state: snapshot barcoding of ventral midbrain at E11 and E15, and **pandaCREST**, which combines barcoding, ex vivo organoid culture and a **clonal splitting strategy** to link a progenitor's in vivo transcriptome with its clone's differentiation potential. Source methods were NOT read (paywall); this is a known H20 gap, stated here.
- Structure seen (pattern sharing between samples, no cell types): each pandaE11 replicate shares 251-326 informative v2 patterns with the OGN replicate of the same number, against 10-32 between unrelated samples (the coincidence baseline). So the pairs (pandaE11_k, OGN_k) are 3 embryos, each split into an in vivo arm and an organoid arm. Amendment 1's rule (pattern in one sample only) had excluded exactly these clones.
- **New mapping:** clone = informative v2 pattern present in pandaE11_k and OGN_k of the same k and in no other sample (patterns seen in an unrelated sample are dropped as coincidence). Arm 1 = its pandaE11 cells (in vivo state at E11), arm 2 = its OGN cells (organoid fate).
- **New estimand (S1, not now):** the arms carry different cell-type vocabularies (progenitors in vivo, derivatives in organoids), so the sister heritable share does not apply. The estimand becomes time-split predictability: how much better a clone's arm-1 composition predicts its arm-2 fate composition than the population does (the CellTag time-split configuration of C17-S1R). It goes in the table as a separate parameter, not as a heritable share. The snapshot samples (E11, E15) have no split and stay out: at most **1 neural system**.
- **Gate (fixed now):** eligible clone = >= 3 cells in arm 1 and >= 4 cells in arm 2. Pass if 0.4 x eligible >= 30 (>= 75 eligible over the 3 embryos). Also reported: eligible clones per embryo and the expected coincidental share (baseline sharing / pair sharing). Pass: seal by clone (balanced_split, strata = embryo), then pre-register S1 with the predictability statistic and its smoke tests. Fail: stop.

### C17-S1C amendment 2 result: gate passed, sealed (2026-11-19)
- Structure only; no cell type read. `c17s1c_crest.py split`: 740 split clones (informative v2 pattern in pandaE11_k and OGN_k only); **308 eligible** (>= 3 in vivo cells, >= 4 organoid cells): 100 / 99 / 109 per embryo; median 4 cells per arm. Expected train eligible 123 >= 30: **gate passed**.
- Coincidence check: matched pairs share 326 / 251 / 321 informative v2 patterns, unrelated pandaE11/OGN pairs 14-24 (mean 18): about **6%** of matched-pair sharing could be coincidental before the "no other sample" filter; that filter removes the coincidences that also occur elsewhere, so the true share is at most 6%. Recorded as a dilution bias toward zero in S1.
- `c17s1c_crest.py seal`: H24 balanced map by clone (salt cellware-crest-split-clone-v1, strata = embryo), committed as partition_maps/partition_crest_split_clone.tsv and registered as partitions.crest_split_clone; data/ext_crest entry in sealed.py; c17s1c_crest.py added to the sealers in check_sealed.py. Units train 296 / A 148 / B 148 / C 148; eligible train 123 / A 59 / B 59 / C 67 (per embryo train 39 / 38 / 46).
- Next (needs its own pre-registration before any fate read): S1 time-split predictability on train (arm-1 composition -> arm-2 fate composition vs the population), with clone-shuffle and planted-signal smoke tests and power from power.py with embryos (3) noted as the top-level unit.

## C17-S1C-S1: time-split predictability in the CRISPR brain split clones, TRAIN clones only (pre-registered 2026-11-19; Bence: "yes" = pre-register the S1 time-split test)
- Serves: C17-S1 (C17-S1R: grow the systems; neural class, 0 systems so far). Script c17s1c_s1.py (reads cells only through partitions.train_only("crest_split_clone", ...) after the clone mapping of c17s1c_crest.split_clones; on the runner it fetches the 2.7 MB GEO table and checks its sha256 against the value recorded at download).
- Estimand: how far a clone's in vivo E11 cell-type composition (arm 1) predicts its organoid cell-type composition (arm 2) beyond the population. Leave-one-out kernel predictability P = 1 - mean ||f2 - f2_hat||^2 / mean ||f2 - population f2||^2, with f2_hat a Gaussian-kernel average of the other clones' f2 weighted by arm-1 similarity (bandwidth = median pairwise squared distance). Null: arm-1 rows permuted within strata embryo x arm-1 size (<= 5 / >= 6) x arm-2 size (<= 7 / >= 8), so embryo and clone-size effects cannot create a signal. Reported: P, P_excess = P - mean null P, one-sided permutation p (9,999 permutations), 95% CI for P_excess from a clone bootstrap within embryo (1,000).
- Readout collapse (fixed now, applied per arm on train): types with >= 5% of the arm's train cells kept, at most 8, the rest pooled as "other".
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: split clone (123 eligible train clones; 39 / 38 / 46 per embryo). No treatment contrast, so H22 does not apply; the 3 embryos are strata, too few to resample, so the CI is over clones within embryo and is stated as conditional on these 3 embryos.
  2. Readout: the cell type column of the barcode table (author annotation); not read so far.
  3. Used data first: CRISPR brain set is new; train only; A/B/C sealed and not touched.
  4. Power (H17, from the statistic's own simulation): synthetic clones on the real train arm sizes (results_c17/c17s1c_sizes.json, structure only), a shared clone latent with between-arm correlation H, arm-specific type loadings (different vocabularies), K = 6 or 8 types. Effect input: H = 0.66, the lowest used heritable share in the table (CellTag LSK, C7-S2); between-clone logit scale sigma = 1.0 is an assumption, not a used result (grid 0.5 / 1.0 / 1.5 reported). **Gate: power >= 0.8 at H 0.66, sigma 1.0 for both K, else stop before any cell type is read.**
  5. Exposure: structure (pattern sharing, arm sizes, partition counts); GEO design text; abstract.
  6. Literature: source methods paywalled (H20 gap recorded at amendment 2). The source's stated claim is that progenitors of one transcriptomic type have heterogeneous clonal fates; our P is a parameter for the table, not a novelty claim (lit/novelty/C17-S1.md covers the cross-system comparison).
  7. Readout gate (H21): >= 30 train clones and >= 2 kept types in each arm, shown by the `readout` stage before `train` runs; else stop.
- Smoke (before any real read): 200 synthetic data sets each, 199 permutations. Nulls (H = 0): plain, with strong embryo offsets, and with a strong clone-size effect on one type in both arms; each must reject at alpha 0.025 in <= 5%. Planted (H 0.9, sigma 1.5) must reject in >= 90%. Fail = INVALID, stop.
- Order: smoke, power, readout, train; each stage runs only if the previous gate passed.
- Prediction (written now): P_excess > 0 but small (0.0-0.15), since arm 1 is an early progenitor snapshot and the source reports heterogeneous fates within types.
- Limits written now: (a) both arms come from one embryo region, so a shared prior history (position in the tissue at E11) counts as memory here; (b) arm-1 types are progenitor states, so P measures state-to-fate predictability (the CellTag time-split configuration), not a sister heritable share; it enters the table as a separate parameter `split_predictability`; (c) up to 6% of clones may be chance pattern matches (amendment 2 result), a dilution toward 0.
- Practice: offline selftest of the statistic (strong vs no memory, collapse rule); synthetic smoke and power on the real arm sizes before any fate read; the train stage reuses the tested functions; 1-stage writer check offline.
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1c_s1.txt), stages as separate lines; selftest offline.

### C17-S1C-S1 smoke and power (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44616024190; synthetic only, no cell type read)
- Smoke (200 sets, alpha 0.025): plain null 4.5%, embryo-offset null 5.0%, size-only null 3.5% (all <= 5%); planted H 0.9 100%. **PASS** (embryo-offset null exactly at the limit).
- Power on the 123 train arm sizes: **H 0.66, sigma 1.0: 0.965 (K 6) / 0.98 (K 8) -> gate passed.** Sensitivity: sigma 0.5 gives 0.53-0.56 at H 0.66 and 0.75-0.77 at H 0.81; H 0.33 gives 0.11-0.61. So a null result would rule out strong, broad between-clone fate bias, not weak bias.
- Next, pre-registered order: `readout` (H21 gate), then `train`.

### C17-S1C-S1 readout gate (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44616950244; train clones only)
- 123 train clones; arm 1 (in vivo E11) 1,291 cells over 14 types, arm 2 (organoid) 1,755 cells over 19 types.
- Kept by the fixed rule (>= 5%): arm 1 six types (progenitor and early neuroblast groups, 85% of cells), arm 2 six types (GABAergic and glutamatergic neuron groups, 68% of cells); the rest pooled as "other". Arm 1 is mostly progenitors/neuroblasts, arm 2 mostly neurons, as the design implies.
- **Gate passed** (>= 30 clones, >= 2 kept types per arm). Next: `train`.

### C17-S1C-S1 result (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44617537758; `results_c17/c17s1c_s1_train.json`; 123 TRAIN clones, nothing sealed read)
- **P 0.224, null mean 0.006, P_excess 0.218, permutation p 0.0001** (the floor at 9,999 permutations). Bootstrap 95% CI [0.18, 0.26]: **not trusted, see 2.**
- Prediction (P_excess 0.0-0.15) **not met**: the value is higher, above every synthetic setting in the power grid (H 0.81, sigma 1.5: 0.15; planted H 0.9: 0.19).
- Self-challenge:
  1. **Suspicious size; what it is.** The type names carry regional identity in both arms (basal-lateral / basal-medial / alar groups, GABAergic vs glutamatergic). An E11 progenitor clone's region and lineage branch decide its neuron type, so most of P is likely positional identity and commitment kept by descent, not plastic state memory. As in the late PEtracer embryos, this is a "commitment" value, not a memory-per-division value.
  2. **The CI is biased (method flaw found after the run).** The bootstrap draws clones with replacement; a duplicated clone matches its own copy at kernel distance 0 in the leave-one-out step, which inflates P in the resample but not in its permutation null. The point estimate and the permutation p are unaffected. Fix needs an amendment (exclude a clone's own copies from its prediction, or resample embryos / jackknife clones); not done.
  3. Other explanations: shared annotation pipeline cannot create a clone-level link by itself (the null keeps both arms' type frequencies); coincidental pattern matches (<= 6%) only dilute; clone size and embryo are controlled by the permutation strata.
  4. Units: 123 clones in 3 embryos; per-embryo values not computed (not pre-registered).
  5. Published? The source states heterogeneous fates within one progenitor type; it addresses the same link from the other side. Our P is a parameter for the table, not a claim.
- **Table:** not added yet; it waits for the CI fix. Planned row: "CRISPR brain split clones (train)", neural class, split_predictability 0.22, with the regional-identity caveat. That would be the first neural system.

### C17-S1C-S1 amendment 1: copy-aware bootstrap CI (2026-11-19; Bence: "yes" = fix the CI; after the result, CI only)
- Changes only the interval; the point estimate (P_excess 0.218) and the permutation p (0.0001) stand as reported.
- Fix: in each bootstrap resample, a clone's copies are excluded from its own prediction (kernel weight 0 between rows of the same original clone) and from its population mean, in the resample's statistic and in its permutation null alike. Resampling stays within embryo, 1,000 resamples x 99 permutations.
- Check before the real run (synthetic, real arm sizes): 40 null data sets (H 0), CI lower bound <= 0 in >= 90% (i.e. the fixed CI does not invent signal), and 40 planted sets (H 0.81, sigma 1.5) where the CI should contain the full-data P_excess in >= 80%. If the check fails, no CI is reported and the table row carries the point only.
- Output: results_c17/c17s1c_s1_ci.json (new stage `ci`; reads train clones only, as `train`).
- Offline note on amendment 1 (synthetic only): the bias is small, because the kernel spreads weight over ~120 clones and a copy gets ~2% of it. On one planted set (H 0.81, sigma 1.5) the naive bootstrap mean was 0.100 against a full-data P_excess of 0.084; the copy-aware mean was 0.078. Expect the fixed CI to shift down by roughly 0.01-0.02, not to change the conclusion.

### C17-S1C-S1 amendment 1 result (2026-11-19; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44618826289; `results_c17/c17s1c_s1_ci.json`; train only)
- Coverage check (40 synthetic sets each): null CI lower bound <= 0 in 100%; planted CI contains the full-data value in 100% (the interval is on the conservative side). **PASS.**
- **Fixed: P_excess 0.218, 95% CI [0.166, 0.247]** (old naive CI [0.181, 0.261]; shifted down about 0.015, as the offline note expected). Point re-check 0.218.
- **Table:** added as "CRISPR brain split clones (train)", class neural progenitor, split_predictability 0.22 [0.17, 0.25], identified, caveats: regional identity kept by descent; state-to-fate configuration, not on the heritable-share scale; 3 embryos. Neural class: **1 system**.

## C17-S1N2: one bounded neural search pass beyond human/mouse and with neural wording (pre-registered 2026-11-20; Bence: "Two more neural systems if it doesnt really take us to a drift and after focus on the Stage-aware memory model")
- Serves: C17-S1 (C17-S1R: grow the systems; neural class has 1 system). Script c17s1n2_neural.py (reuses c17_data_sweep.esearch/get and c17s1n_struct.check/design), on Actions.
- Why: the C17-S1D sweep searched human and mouse only and had no neural-specific query; the cerebral organoid scar-recording set (BioStudies E-MTAB-10971) appeared as a hit but was never checked for design.
- **Made exhaustive before any run** (Bence: "you cannot miss anything: The earlier sweep missed neural-specific data - do it more robust"). Retrieval: GEO, any organism, since 2012, four queries (neural topic x lineage terms; lineage method names with no topic limit, e.g. GESTALT, LINNAEUS, iTracer, STICR, TrackerSeq, TREX, CloneSeq, MADM, CellTag, LARRY, CARLIN/DARLIN, MEMOIR, PEtracer, CREST, Polylox, Confetti, CRISPR/Cas9/evolving/viral barcodes; neural x sister/split/two-colour; neural x barcode x organoid/time course), up to 2,000 ids each; BioStudies/ArrayExpress and Zenodo with 12 neural lineage phrasings, up to 3 pages of 100 each. Pre-filter: neural wording AND a clone/lineage/tree/sister term in title or summary. **No cap**: every pre-filtered series is checked (GEO series + sample text; BioStudies study JSON; Zenodo title + description only, verdict "check").
- **Recall gate:** every neural set already known (GSE210139, GSE327468, GSE300285, GSE300287, GSE300289, GSE324903, GSE324905, E-MTAB-10971) must be retrieved and pass the pre-filter; any miss = pass INVALID, queries widened and re-run before any verdict is used.
- **Bound (anti-drift):** metadata only, no download, one pass (plus a re-run only if recall fails); then the stage-aware model, whatever the result. Non-neural memory-capable hits are not acted on.
- Rule (stricter than C17-S1N, fixed now, because "scar" also means glial scar): memory-capable = sister split, OR serial sampling of the same clones at >= 2 timepoints, OR a tree term together with a clone/barcode term. Sets already checked (C17-S1N) and sealed sets are skipped. Titles pass lit_gap.neutral before saving; excluded ones are counted only.
- Pre-flight: unit = data series; readout = design terms only (no data); used data first: none used; power: not a test; exposure: metadata only; literature: none read; readout gate: n/a.
- Output: results_c17/c17s1n2_neural.json with verdicts. A memory-capable hit becomes a candidate only; download size, Bence's OK for > 2 GB, and sealing by clone come before any statistic.
- Practice: offline selftest of the stricter rule (glial-scar text must not pass; a scar-array lineage text must pass).
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1n2.txt).

- Serves: C17-S1 (C17-S1R: grow the systems; neural class has 1 system, the law test needs 3). Script c17s1g_gates.py (stages `fetch`, `schema`, `madm`, `gate <candidate>`, `selftest`).
