  - **G2 zebrafish developing brain, scar-array trees** (GSE105010 RAW.tar 5.8 MB: per-fish barcode files; GSE158142 F8-F15 GestMaster tables, < 1 MB): one system family.
  - **G3 zebrafish adult brain, scar lineage tracing** (GSE246714: the 10 `filtered_scars` tables of lineage replicates 1 and 2, GSM-level files).
  - **G4 human cerebral organoids, iTracer** (E-MTAB-10971, 10973, 10974: `meta*.tsv.gz` only, about 4.6 MB). These tables also hold cell-type columns: the `schema` stage lists column names and types only; type-like columns (CREST FATE_LIKE rule) are never tabulated.
  - **G5 SPACE-seq developing brain** (GSE327687 RAW.tar 0.5 MB, brain samples only; the liver series GSE326431 and the tumour samples are an excluded domain and are not opened).
- Units and arms, fixed now:
  - G1: clone = title prefix; the two MADM colours would be the arms, but colour is not in the metadata; upper bound first: clones with >= 4 cells. Fail if that bound is < 75.
  - G2, G3, G5 (cumulative edits): within one animal (or section), a clade = all cells carrying a given edit that occurs in >= 2 distinct full alleles and in < 50% of that animal's lineage-called cells (not a founder edit); its two largest distinct full alleles are the two arms. Clades are taken smallest first; a clade that shares cells with one already taken is skipped (disjoint pairs, as C17-S1P).
  - G4: clone = static iTracer barcode within an organoid; arms = its two largest distinct scar alleles.
  - Eligible pair or clone: both arms >= 4 cells (C7-S2 primary arm size; G1 bound as stated).
- **Gate per candidate: pass if 0.4 x eligible >= 30 (>= 75 eligible units).** Also reported: units per animal/organoid, the coincidence check where alleles can recur across animals (share of full alleles seen in > 1 animal).
- Order: `fetch` (sha256 written to SHA256SUMS in each data/ext_* directory, and a sealed.py DATASETS entry "structure only until partitioned"), then `schema`, then the column mapping for each candidate is written as an amendment **before** `gate` runs (the file formats are not known yet), then `gate`. A pass leads to sealing by unit (balanced_split, strata = animal/organoid) before any fate read; a fail stops that candidate.
- Pre-flight: unit as above; readout = structure only (edits, alleles, counts); used data first: none of these sets is used; power: the gate; exposure: column names, allele structure and counts only; literature: GEO/BioStudies text only, source methods not read (H20 gap, recorded); readout gate (H21) = the gate above.
- Limits written now: arms from nested edits are subclades of one clade, not separated sister wells; G2/G3/G5 values will be upper bounds as in C17-S1P (shared niche). G5 spatial beads may mix cells; that is checked at S1, not here.
- Practice: offline selftest of the clade picker (toy alleles with a founder edit, two nested clades, an overlapping clade that must be skipped) and of the title parser; downloads read with python -I from their own directories.
- Compute: local (downloads about 15 MB; structure counts under 2 minutes); no fate column is read.

### C17-S1G G1 result and schema (2026-11-20; structure only)
- **G1 MADM-CloneSeq: FAIL.** GEO titles give 45 clones at E10 (median 8 cells) and none parseable at E12; clones with >= 4 cells = 39 < 75, before colour is even considered. Stop.
- **G5 SPACE-seq: FAIL (no data).** The series archive holds only the tumour samples' allele tables; no brain lineage table is deposited (listing only; archive deleted unopened).
- Schema (`results_c17/c17s1g_schema.json`): G2 per-cell lineage tables = GSE105010 ZF1-ZF3 GestMaster (inside RAW.tar) and GSE158142 F8-F15 GestMaster, column `HMID` (sites joined by "-"); the hsp*.allReadCounts files carry no cell barcode and are not used. G3 = tab-separated scar reads (Reads, CIGAR, Barcode, UMI, Location, Sequence) at 6 endogenous target sites, 2 animals. G4 = `GeneBarcodeMerge(d)` (static clone barcode) and `ScarMerge(d)` (scar allele) per cell, organoid id in `organoid` / `orig.ident` / `sample`.
- **Exposure note:** the schema printed one example value for columns my type-name filter missed (a neuron-vs-progenitor score, pseudotime, atlas projection flags and cluster numbers); single values only, nothing tabulated. The filter now prints examples only for ID and lineage columns.

### C17-S1G amendment 1: column mapping (written before any gate count)
- G2: animal = fish file (11 fish); full allele = `HMID`; edits = position:site value for sites not NONE/UNKNOWN (sites split on "-").
- G3: animal = lineage replicate (lin1, lin2); per cell and target site, scars = distinct (Location, CIGAR) with >= 2 reads whose CIGAR has an I or D (pure-match CIGAR = unedited, dropped); edits = site:Location:CIGAR; full allele = sorted join of the cell's edits; cells with edits at >= 2 sites only.
- G4: E-MTAB-10971 is a gene-perturbation set and is **excluded** (perturbation confounds memory); used: E-MTAB-10973 (organoid id `orig.ident`), E-MTAB-10974 org1-12 (`organoid`; only cells of the most common `genotype` level, read as a design label) and d15 (`sample`). Clone = organoid + static barcode; arms = its two largest distinct scar alleles that carry >= 1 edit (an all-match scar string = unedited, not an arm).
- Gates unchanged (both arms >= 4 cells; pass if 0.4 x eligible >= 30).

### C17-S1G result (2026-11-20; local structure counts, `results_c17/c17s1g_gate_*.json`; no fate column read)
- **G2 zebrafish developing brain: FAIL.** 11 fish, 9,525 cells with an HMID; 338 disjoint clade pairs, **38 eligible** (both arms >= 4 cells; ZF2 alone 17), expected train 15 < 30. 21% of full alleles recur in > 1 fish (common GESTALT outcomes), so some clades would be coincidence anyway.
- **G3 zebrafish adult brain: FAIL.** 5,685 cells with edits at >= 2 sites (2 animals); 172 clade pairs, **0 eligible**. Under the fixed mapping a cell's full allele is the exact set of its called scars, and site dropout makes nearly every full allele unique, so arms stay at 1-3 cells. A dropout-tolerant mapping was not tried (it would be a new forking choice; not without Bence's OK).
- **G4 iTracer organoids: FAIL.** 17 organoids/sections, 4,079 barcode clones, **19 eligible** (two scarred alleles with >= 4 cells each); most clones carry no or one scar allele at this depth. The genotype filter kept 44% of org1-12 cells (most common level).
- With G1 and G5: **all 5 candidates fail**. The neural class stays at **1 system** (CRISPR brain split clones). The search (C17-S1N2, recall-checked) and these gates exhaust the public neural sets found; no rule was relaxed after seeing counts.
- Self-challenge: is >= 4 cells per arm too strict? It is the standard used for every system in the table (C7-S2 primary arm size); lowering it now would be chosen after seeing counts. Near miss: G2 at 38 of 75.
- Next (Bence 2026-11-20): the stage-aware memory model.

## C17-S1T: stage-aware memory model, commitment vs per-division memory on the embryo trees, TRAIN embryos only (pre-registered 2026-11-20; Bence: "Yes, pre-register")
- **Serves: C17-S1T** (FOCUS step; novelty lit/novelty/C17-S1T.md with Bence: "Yes, proceed"; H20 lit/c17s1t_h20_2026-11-20.md). Script c17s1t_stage.py, reusing c14s0_gate.load_obs / iter_train_trees (train embryos filtered with partitions.train_only before any other column; other partitions skipped by key before parsing) and the C17-S1P pair picker extended to return depths. EXPLORATORY on train; no sealed read, no claim.
- **Overlap stated up front:** C16-S1 already fitted, on the same train trees but only for the paraxial-vs-lateral split, transition rates that fall about 5-fold with depth plus an inherited hidden bias (half-life about 10 edges). New here: all lineage labels (14), commitment and memory as explicit nested reductions of one model, and the memory value on the per-division scale of the parameter table (LARRY rho_div). On these trees this is largely a re-parameterisation of C16-S1; the new part is the nested test and the table-scale value.
- **Model (closed form, pair level).** A sister-subclade pair has its MRCA at tau edges from its tree root and k = mean edges from the MRCA to the pair's labelled leaves. Expected cross-arm label agreement a = sum_j f1_j f2_j:
  - a(tau, k) = Q + (1 - Q) * (1 - eps) * [C(tau) + (1 - C(tau)) * lambda^(2k)], with Q = the embryo's sum of squared lineage fractions (random-pair agreement), C(tau) = logistic(alpha + beta * tau) the probability that the lineage was committed by the MRCA, lambda the memory kept per edge, eps a label-noise term.
  - **M_mem** (stationary memory, PATH / kin-correlation case): C = 0, so a depends on k only.
  - **M_com** (commitment without memory, fate-mapping case): lambda = 0, so a depends on tau only.
  - **M_full**: both. Generative version for synthetic data: each pair draws a shared label L ~ embryo fractions; each arm cell takes L with probability s = sqrt(C + (1 - C) lambda^(2k)), else a draw from the fractions; then label noise eps. E[a] equals the closed form exactly.
  - Fit: weighted least squares on per-pair a (weights n1 * n2, capped at the 95th percentile), 5 starts, best kept.
- **Primary statistic:** leave-one-embryo-out held-out weighted squared error per pair, M_full vs each reduction, per embryo with >= 30 pairs.
- **Rule:** STAGE-AWARE MODEL SUPPORTED (exploratory) if M_full has lower held-out error than BOTH reductions in all but at most one eligible embryo. Otherwise report which reduction suffices.
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: disjoint sister-subclade pair, clustered in embryos (7 train embryos: E7.5 1, E8.0 2, E8.5 2, E9.0 1, E9.5 1); the test unit is the held-out embryo. No treatment contrast, so H22 does not apply; stage enters only through tau, and no between-stage contrast is claimed.
  2. Readout: obs `lineage` labels per subclade (used on train in C14/C16/C17-S1P); MRCA depth and leaf depth in edges (used in C16).
  3. Used data first: train embryos only; A spent, B/C sealed, skipped by key before parsing.
  4. Power (H19/H17, from the statistic's own simulation on the real train structure): synthetic labels on the real (embryo, tau, k, n1, n2) pairs. Effect inputs from used results: lambda 0.935 per edge (C16-S1 half-life 10.3 edges); eps from C17-S1P D_noise (0.09 as a fraction of D_rand 0.77, i.e. eps about 0.12); C(tau) rising from 0.1 to 0.9 across the 10th-90th percentile of train tau (assumption, shaped on the C17-S1P stage rise -0.01 to 0.89). Spent results that constrain inputs: C16-S0/S1 (memory and depth-varying rates on P/L), C17-S1P (H by stage). **Gate: power of the rule >= 0.8 at lambda 0.935 with the full commitment slope; also reported at lambda 0.85 / 0.97 and half slope. Below 0.8: stop before the fit.**
  5. Exposure: as C14/C16/C17-S1P (train cells, trees, labels).
  6. Literature: H20 done (PATH, quantitative fate mapping, kin correlation, Phillips 2019, BMC Biol 2024); the source of the embryo set stays at claims level.
  7. Readout gate (H21): the `structure` stage shows pair counts per embryo, the tau and k distributions and their within-embryo correlation (structure only, no labels); >= 30 pairs in >= 5 embryos, and the smoke below shows the statistic differs between models. Else stop.
- **Smoke (synthetic, real structure, 50 sets each):** truth M_mem: the rule must pass in <= 10%; truth M_com: <= 10%; truth M_full at the power inputs: parameter recovery |lambda_hat - lambda| <= 0.05 in >= 80% (else lambda is not identified on these trees: stop and report). Analytic check: mean simulated a matches the closed form within 0.01 per tau x k bin.
- **Order:** selftest (offline) -> structure -> smoke + power -> fit; each stage runs only if the previous gate passed.
- **Prediction (written now):** M_full beats both reductions in >= 5 of the eligible embryos; lambda between 0.90 and 0.97 per edge; C(tau) rising. E7.5 may not be eligible (few pairs).
- **Limits written now:** (a) sisters in an embryo share a niche, so lambda here is memory plus shared surroundings (upper bound on intrinsic memory, as C17-S1P); (b) edges are edit events, a proxy for divisions; (c) tau and k are partly collinear within an embryo (tau + k is about the leaf depth), so identification leans on unbalanced trees and on the 7 embryos' different depths, which is why recovery is gated; (d) 7 embryos, train only, no claim.
- **Output to the table (if the rule passes and lambda is recovered):** a row "PEtracer embryo trees (train), memory per edge at commitment C = 0", next to LARRY rho_div; the cross-system comparison at matched commitment is pre-registered separately, after this step, with its own power (systems as units, H19).
- Practice: offline selftest of the extended pair picker (toy tree with known tau and k) and of the closed form against the generative simulator; cold start (5 starts, spread reported); analytic regime (closed form vs simulation per bin); measurement physics (edges are edits, label noise eps fitted); adequacy gate (held-out calibration per tau x k bin reported); tick-list in the result entry.
- Compute: GitHub Actions run (sweeps/c17s1t.txt, `--petracer`), stages as separate lines; selftest offline.

### C17-S1T structure, smoke and power (2026-11-20; runs https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44745695335 (structure), https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44748047833 (smoke); train structure only, no pair agreement computed)
- Selftest (offline): same pairs as the C17-S1P picker; closed form vs simulator 0.0004; toy lambda 0.941 (true 0.935).
- **Structure / readout gate: PASS.** 11,057 disjoint pairs (= C17-S1P), all 7 train embryos eligible (48, 158, 218, 870, 913, 2,758, 6,092 pairs; E7.5 to E9.5). tau 3-25 edges (10th-90th 8-16), k 2.0-5.4 (10th-90th 2.4-3.6). tau-k correlation within embryo -0.02 to -0.20, so the two axes are not collinear.
- **Smoke and power (50 synthetic sets per truth, real structure): GATE PASS** (`results_c17/c17s1t_gate.json`).
  - False pass: truth memory-only 0.00, truth commitment-only **0.10 (at the limit)**.
  - Truth full (lambda 0.935, full slope): rule passes 0.94; lambda recovered within 0.05 in 1.00 (median 0.934); closed form vs simulation, mean max bin difference 0.009 (limit 0.01).
  - Grid: lambda 0.85 power 1.00, lambda 0.97 0.68, half commitment slope 0.62 (recovery 1.00, 1.00, 0.92).
- Reading: the test can tell the three models apart and recover lambda on these trees at the planted values; it is weak if memory is very long (lambda 0.97) or commitment rises slowly; the commitment-only false pass at 0.10 means a narrow pass (exactly 6/7) would need caution.
- Next, pre-registered order: `fit` (train), waits for Bence's go.

### C17-S1T result (2026-11-20; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44753852098; `results_c17/c17s1t_fit.json`; Bence: "Go with 1"; 7 TRAIN embryos, nothing sealed read; EXPLORATORY)
- **Verdict by the pre-registered rule: NOT SUPPORTED.** M_full beat both reductions in **4 of 7** embryos (E8.0-R1, E8.5-R2, E8.5-R3, E9.5-R1); the rule needed 6.
- Held-out weighted squared error (mem / com / full): E7.5-R1 0.255 / **0.132** / 0.135; E8.0-R1 0.272 / 0.1724 / **0.1720**; E8.0-R3 0.272 / **0.1716** / 0.1718; E8.5-R2 0.189 / 0.162 / **0.160**; E8.5-R3 0.190 / 0.180 / **0.176**; E9.0-R1 **0.130** / 0.135 / 0.135; E9.5-R1 0.131 / 0.106 / **0.104**.
- **Which reduction suffices: commitment-only.** It is within 0-2% of M_full in every embryo and beats memory-only in 6/7 (by 5-50%). Memory adds at most 2% held-out error reduction (E8.5-R3), in 4 embryos.
- Full-data fits (start spread < 1e-7): M_full lambda **0.86** per edge (LOEO 0.84-0.88), eps 0.14, C(tau) 0.33 / 0.64 / 0.94 at tau 8 / 11 / 16 edges. M_mem alone: lambda 0.94, eps 0. M_com: eps 0.13.
- Prediction: >= 5 embryos (met: no, 4); lambda 0.90-0.97 (no, 0.86); C rising (yes).
- Calibration (in sample, M_full, tau x k tertiles): in the shallowest-tau tertile the observed agreement falls faster with k (0.685 -> 0.669 -> 0.553) than the model (0.648 -> 0.617 -> 0.581); in deeper tertiles the fit is within 0.03. Not pre-registered as a test; noted only.
- Self-challenge:
  1. Suspicious? The smoke gave power 0.94 at lambda 0.935, so a fail is informative about that setting: on these trees the k-dependence (memory) is small next to the tau-dependence (commitment). The fitted lambda (0.86) sits where the synthetic power was 1.00, yet the reductions tie, because the memory term moves agreement little over k 2-5 edges once C(tau) is fitted.
  2. Other explanations: (a) the k range is narrow (10th-90th 2.4-3.6 edges), so memory beyond a few edges is not seen; (b) shared niche and commitment are both absorbed by C(tau); (c) E9.0-R1 prefers memory-only, so the tau-to-commitment map does not transfer perfectly between embryos (tree depth calibration differs per embryo); (d) the shallow-tau calibration gap hints that memory matters mainly before commitment, which one global lambda averages away.
  3. Units: 7 embryos; per-embryo differences between com and full are 0.0002-0.004, small.
  4. Used data enough? All 11,057 train pairs.
  5. Already published? Commitment dominating fate agreement on embryo trees is in line with quantitative fate mapping (commitment without memory) and the source study's restriction timing (claims level).
- **Table:** no row added (pre-registered: only if the rule passes). The C17-S1P row (H 0.81, stage-dependent) stands with its caveat; this result says that value is mostly commitment, not per-division memory.

### C17-S1T follow-up check: memory at commitment near zero (2026-11-20; Bence: "Go with 1"; log read only, no data, no compute)
- Before pre-registering a new fit on LARRY and the gastruloids, the log was checked: **this comparison already exists (C5-S2, 2026-11-07, K1 FAIL).** Blood (LARRY E19c, cytokine wells, about 4 extra divisions): rho_div 0.964 [0.927, 0.997]; gastruloid subclones (G5): no per-division loss allowed (rho_div >= 1.00), memory is lost at passage events instead (retention 0.46 per passage). The intervals do not overlap, so one per-division law already failed across these two systems at C near 0.
- A new fit on the same data would repeat C5-S2, so none was pre-registered (H16: no duplicate work).
- Combined reading with the C17-S1T result: in embryo trees, sister agreement is mostly commitment (memory adds <= 2%); where commitment is near zero, memory per division differs between blood (decays slowly) and gastruloids (kept through divisions, lost at passages). A stage-aware model with one lambda does not unify the systems; memory loss is tied to events (passage, commitment) more than to division count.

### C17-S1T follow-up 2: events vs divisions inside CellTag LSK, pre-flight STOP at S0 (2026-11-20; Bence: "1"; structure read of train clone sizes only, no fate labels, local, Opus 5.5)
- Question: within one blood system, is memory lost per division (agreement falls with clone expansion) or at commitment (no size effect once differentiation is accounted for)? Design considered: day-5 sister wells, per-clone heritable share vs log2 clone size (division proxy), conditioned on differentiation.
- Pre-flight (H15/H19), on train clone sizes only (440 train clones with >= 2 cells in both wells):
  1. Division proxy is narrow and noisy: log2 clone size 10th-90th 2.3-4.8 (about 2.4 doublings); log2 size of well 1 vs well 2 correlates only 0.30, so per-arm division count is poorly read.
  2. Power (rough, from the C7-S2a bootstrap SE 0.028 at n 342; size halves differ by 1.5 doublings): at LARRY's rho_div 0.964 the expected H difference is 0.08 (SE 0.056), **power 0.29 on train, 0.60 even if A+B+C were all spent**; only at rho_div 0.927 (LARRY lower bound) does train reach 0.78. Below the 0.8 gate in every setting that keeps sealed data.
  3. Confound: differentiated clones expand more, so clone size and commitment move together; the test cannot separate them in this culture.
  4. Exposure: the size hint came from this same train data (C7-S2a: H 0.75 at >= 2 cells vs 0.66 at >= 4), so a train-only test would be circular.
- **Decision: stop at S0, nothing pre-registered, no script written.** Sealed partitions A/B/C of celltag_lsk stay unspent. The events-vs-divisions reading stays a cross-system observation (C5-S2 + C17-S1T), untested within one system.

## C17-S1PL: dated whole-embryo tree (DNA Typewriter mouse), S0 structure gate and sealing before any fate read (pre-registered 2026-11-20; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C17-S1PL** (FOCUS step; novelty lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md, with Published but proceeding: Bence: "1"). Scripts c17s1pl_tree.py (new; stages `fetch`, `schema`, `gate`, `seal`, `selftest`), reusing the C17-S1P / C17-S1T pair picker logic (c17s1p_trees.pairs_of, c17s1t_stage.pairs_of) re-implemented with counts instead of leaf lists for a 1.28M-leaf tree (selftest: same pairs as c17s1p_trees.pairs_of on toy trees). Routing (smart delegation): Opus writes this gate and the script; Sonnet `cellware-data` downloads, checksums and runs `schema`; `gate` runs on Actions.
- **Why this set:** C17-S1T could not separate per-division memory from commitment on the sealed embryo trees, partly because divisions since a split spanned only 2.4-3.6 edges (10th-90th). This tree is one embryo, dated, zygote-rooted, with 1.28M profiled cells (source paper, claims level), so splits of many ages are available. Sibling cell-type agreement on it is published (input only).
- **Data:** public GitHub repo shendurelab/dtt-mouse, release tag v1.1.0: `support_data/merged_minB2h_lineage_constrained.nwk` (dated, lineage-constrained tree, 34.0 MB) and `support_data/cell_metadata.v8.txt.gz` (57.0 MB) -> data/ext_dtt_mouse/raw, SHA256SUMS there, sha256 constants committed in the script; sealed.py entry "structure only until partitioned". Not downloaded: the full placed tree, the consensus table, the GEO expression matrices.
- **Exposure rules:** the metadata table holds cell-type columns. `schema` prints column names and dtypes, and example values only for ID-like columns (C17-S1G fix). No type-like column is read or tabulated before sealing. A leaf counts as "labelled" if its ID joins a metadata row (ID column only).
- **Units:** sister-clade pair = the two largest children of a node, both with >= 4 labelled leaves; disjoint pairs, smallest clades first (C17-S1P rule). Primary clade cap 3,000 leaves (raised from 300 because the point is a wide range of split ages; written before any count); cap 300 reported for comparison. tau = node depth in edges from the root; k = mean edges from the node to its labelled leaves; time since split = mean root-to-leaf branch length minus the node's root distance (units as in the file; reported, not gated).
- **Sealing unit (fixed now):** founder clade = maximal clade with <= 20,000 leaves; strata = the two daughters of the first cleavage (the root's two largest children; the source calls them inline replicates). Balanced split (H24, salt cellware-dtt-founder-v1), train 40% / A, B, C 20% each, committed as partition_maps/partition_dtt_founder.tsv, before any cell type is read.
- **Gate (all must pass; else stop and report):**
  - G1: eligible pairs (cap 3,000) >= 75 (0.4 x eligible >= 30).
  - G2: the 10th-90th percentile range of k >= 2.4 edges (twice the sealed embryo set's 1.2); otherwise this tree gives no more leverage than C17-S1T.
  - G3: founder clades holding >= 1 eligible pair >= 50 (so each sealed partition holds >= 10).
  - G4: |corr(tau, k)| over eligible pairs <= 0.8 (tau and k not collinear).
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: sister-clade pair, clustered in founder clades; one embryo, so no between-embryo claim; the test unit for the later fit is the founder clade (H22 does not apply: no treatment).
  2. Readout: tree topology, branch lengths, leaf IDs and the metadata ID join; no outcome.
  3. Used data first: this set is new; C17-S1T on the used embryo train trees came first and was not supported.
  4. Power: not a test; the gate is structural. Power for the re-registered C17-S1T test comes from its own smoke on this tree's real structure, with founder clades as units.
  5. Exposure: source paper abstract only (novelty file); column names; counts.
  6. Literature: H20 for the model is lit/c17s1t_h20_2026-11-20.md; source-paper methods for tree building not read beyond the repo README (stated gap).
  7. Readout gate (H21): G1-G4.
- **Prediction (written now):** G1 and G3 pass easily; G2 is the real question (deep clades are large, the cap may bind); G4 passes.
- Limits written now: one embryo (no replication across embryos; the first-cleavage halves are the only internal replicate); sisters share a niche (upper bound on intrinsic memory, as C17-S1P); the lineage-constrained tree used cell-type information in its construction (repo name "lineage_constrained"), which could inflate sibling agreement: the later fit must say so, and the unconstrained NJ backbone stays a fallback check.
- Practice: offline selftest of the count-based picker against c17s1p_trees.pairs_of on toy trees, and of the Newick parser on a toy dated tree; downloads read with python -I from their own directory; large reads on Actions; neutral wording.
- Compute: `fetch` and `schema` local (Sonnet, small reads); `gate` and `seal` on GitHub Actions (sweeps/c17s1pl_gate.txt; the runner downloads by tag and checks sha256).

### C17-S1PL amendment 1: column mapping and pinned files (2026-11-20; written before any gate count)
- Fetch and schema ran locally on the Sonnet `cellware-data` lane (fetch 36 s, schema 4 s). Tree 33,984,975 B, sha256 dcc12fcd...aa79; metadata 57,035,367 B, sha256 208dc0a0...4058; both pinned in c17s1pl_tree.py, so the Actions runner re-downloads by tag and verifies.
- Metadata: 1,584,848 rows, 9 columns (an ID, two trajectory/type columns, five embedding coordinates, one mapping column). Example values were printed for the ID column only; no type column was read.
- Mapping: ID_COL = `cell_id`, which has the same format as the tree leaf names. A leaf is "labelled" if its name is a `cell_id`. Gates G1-G4 unchanged.

### C17-S1PL gate result: FAIL on G2, stop (2026-11-20; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44795416993; `results_c17/c17s1pl_gate.json`; structure only, no cell type read, nothing sealed)
- Tree: 1,304,629 nodes, **655,701 leaves** (the dated lineage-constrained tree holds about half of the 1.28M profiled cells; the source's count refers to the full placed tree), all joined to `cell_id`; branch lengths on every edge. First-cleavage halves 410,925 / 244,776 leaves. 93 founder clades.
- G1 PASS: 26,731 disjoint eligible pairs. G3 PASS: 91 founder clades hold pairs. G4 PASS: corr(tau, k) 0.01.
- **G2 FAIL: k 10th-90th 3.25-5.06 edges, range 1.81 < 2.4.** It is wider than the sealed embryo set (1.2) but below the pre-registered bar. Stop by the rule; no sealing, no type read.
- Time since split (branch-length units, read as days): 10th-90th 1.45-5.47, a 3.8-fold spread, far wider than the edge spread. G2 was fixed on edges, so this does not change the verdict.
- **Design flaw found by the result:** caps 3,000 and 300 give identical pairs, because the smallest-first disjoint rule takes the smallest clades first, so the cap never binds and old splits are never picked. The pre-registered prediction ("the cap may bind") was wrong. A picker that samples splits across ages (e.g. strata of node date) would be a new design choice and needs Bence's OK as an amendment. No rule is relaxed here.
- Self-challenge: is G2 too strict? It was fixed before any count, at twice the old range, and the result is 1.81. Lowering it now would be chosen after seeing the count. The time spread is a real lead, but the C17-S1T model counts divisions in edges.

### C17-S1PL amendment 2: split-age-stratified picker (2026-11-20; Bence: "1"; written after the G2 fail, before any new count)
- Cause of the fail (amendment 1 result): the smallest-first disjoint rule only reaches recent splits, so the cap never binds.
- **One change: the picker.** Candidates are as before (node with <= 3,000 leaves, two largest children each with >= 4 labelled leaves). They are split into 5 equal-count bins by node date (root distance). Within each bin the order is fixed by sha256("cellware-dtt-pick-v1:" + node). The picker then takes candidates round-robin across bins (bin 1, 2, ..., 5, 1, ...), skipping any that overlap an already picked clade. So old and recent splits are both represented.
- **Unchanged:** G1-G4 and their thresholds, G2 on edges (the C17-S1T model counts divisions in edges), founder clades, sealing. Time-since-split spread is reported, not gated. The old smallest-first picker is reported alongside for comparison.
- Forking-path count: this is the second picker tried on this tree; any later step states it. If G2 still fails, the step closes; no third picker.
- Selftest: the picks are disjoint, every bin is represented on a toy tree, and the result is deterministic.

### C17-S1PL amendment 2 result: gate PASS, sealed by founder clade (2026-11-20; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44798786231; `results_c17/c17s1pl_gate2.json`; structure only, no cell type read)
- **Stratified picker: all four gates pass.**
  - G1: 19,346 pairs.
  - G2: k 10th-50th-90th 3.44 / 4.62 / 7.33 edges, range **3.89** (bar 2.4; the sealed embryo set had 1.2).
  - G3: 91 founder clades hold pairs.
  - G4: corr(tau, k) -0.10.
  - Also: tau 18-35 edges; time since split 1.88-5.84; clade size 10th-90th 9-47 leaves; median 7 labelled cells per arm.
- The smallest-first picker reproduced gate 1 exactly (26,731 pairs, range 1.81), so the runs are deterministic.
- **Sealed before any cell type read:** `c17s1pl_tree.py seal` (local, 12 s), H24 balanced map by founder clade, strata = first-cleavage half (410,925 / 244,776 leaves). 93 founder clades: train 38, A 19, B 18, C 18. Committed as partition_maps/partition_dtt_founder.tsv and registered as partitions.dtt_founder; the first write used a 3-column format the registry cannot read and was rewritten (same split, verified). Pairs per partition are not counted yet.
- Forking path: 2 pickers tried on this tree (amendment 2 rule: no third).
- Next (not started; needs Bence's go): re-register the C17-S1T nested test (M_mem / M_com / M_full) on train founder clades, with smoke and power simulated on this tree's real structure, founder clades as units (H17/H19).

## C17-S1PL-T: stage-aware memory model (C17-S1T nested test) on the dated embryo tree, TRAIN founder clades only (pre-registered 2026-11-20; Bence: "Go with 1")
- **Serves: C17-S1PL** (FOCUS step; novelty lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md finding 2; Published but proceeding: Bence: "1" for finding 1, an input only). Script c17s1pl_fit.py (new; stages `selftest`, `structure`, `smoke <truth>`, `gate`, `fit`). It reuses unchanged from c17s1t_stage.py: predict, closed_form, fit, weights, simulate, planted_c, TRUTHS, EPS. It reuses from c17s1pl_tree.py: parser, structure, the stratified picker (amendment 2) and founders. Train founder clades are filtered with partitions.train_only before any label is read. Sealed founders' metadata rows are skipped by row index and never parsed.
- **Data:** DNA Typewriter tree (one E13.5 embryo), 38 train founder clades, pairs from the stratified picker. **Label = `major_trajectory`** (the coarse lineage column, the analogue of the embryo set's 14 lineage labels; fixed now, before its levels are seen). Levels holding < 1% of train labelled cells are pooled as "other". Missing values are dropped, and an arm needs >= 4 non-missing labels.
- **Model:** as C17-S1T. a(tau, k) = Q + (1 - Q)(1 - eps)[C(tau) + (1 - C(tau)) lambda^(2k)]. Q is the founder clade's sum of squared label fractions, tau is node depth in edges, and k is the mean edges to the pair's labelled leaves. Nested reductions M_mem (C = 0) and M_com (lambda = 0); weighted least squares (n1 n2, capped at the 95th percentile), 5 starts.
- **Primary statistic:** leave-one-founder-out held-out weighted squared error per eligible founder clade (>= 30 pairs).
- **Rule (fixed now; with 38 units, "all but one" is replaced):** STAGE-AWARE MODEL SUPPORTED (exploratory) if M_full has lower held-out error than both reductions in >= 2/3 of eligible founder clades, AND its pooled held-out error is lower than each reduction's. Otherwise report which reduction suffices.
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: the founder clade (38 train), the test unit for leave-one-out; one embryo. No treatment, so H22 does not apply.
  2. Readout: `major_trajectory` labels of train leaves (first read of any label column on this set, train only); tree depths.
  3. Used data first: C17-S1T on the used embryo train trees came first (not supported, k range too narrow).
  4. Power (H17/H19): synthetic labels on the real train structure (founder, tau, k, n1, n2, founder label fractions), the same 6 truths and gates as C17-S1T. False pass <= 0.10 under memory-only and under commitment-only; power >= 0.8 at lambda 0.935 with the full commitment slope; lambda recovered within 0.05 in >= 80%; closed form vs simulation <= 0.01 per tau x k bin. 50 sets per truth. **Below the gate: stop before the fit.**
  5. Exposure: source abstract; structure counts; the founder label fractions read in `structure` (train only, as C17-S1T's embryo label counts). No pair agreement computed before the gate.
  6. Literature: H20 lit/c17s1t_h20_2026-11-20.md; novelty lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md.
  7. Readout gate (H21): >= 20 eligible founder clades with >= 30 pairs each, and train pairs >= 1,000; else stop.
- **Prediction (written now):** commitment dominates again (C17-S1T, source claims); with the wider k range, lambda is identified. The rule may still fail if M_com is within noise of M_full. If it passes, lambda per edge is between 0.80 and 0.95.
- Limits written now:
  - One embryo; sisters share a niche (upper bound on intrinsic memory).
  - The tree is "lineage-constrained": if cell types shaped its topology, sibling agreement and the commitment term are inflated, which biases toward M_com. The fit must state this, and an unconstrained-tree check is the follow-up if the result depends on it.
  - k in edges is a proxy for divisions. Time since split is reported, not tested.
  - 2 pickers were tried on this tree (amendment 2).
- **Output to the table** (only if the rule passes and lambda is recovered in the smoke): a row "DNA Typewriter mouse (train), memory per edge at commitment C = 0", scale = memory per division.
- Practice: offline selftest (preorder subtree ranges vs explicit descent on toy trees, the label-row skip, the rule function); cold start (5 starts, spread reported); analytic regime check (closed form vs simulation per bin); measurement physics (label noise eps fitted); adequacy (held-out calibration per tau x k bin reported); neutral wording; tick-list in the result entry.
- Compute: GitHub Actions (sweeps/c17s1pl_t_structure.txt, c17s1pl_t_smoke.txt; each line fetches by tag and checks sha256); selftest offline; the fit waits for Bence's go after the gate.

### C17-S1PL-T structure, smoke and power: gate FAILS on the analytic check only; stop before the fit (2026-11-20; runs https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44800715074 (structure), https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44800975551 (smoke); synthetic labels on the real train structure; no pair agreement computed)
- **Readout gate PASS:** 8,146 train pairs; 27 of 38 train founder clades have >= 30 pairs (pair counts per founder range 1 to 602). k 10th-90th 3.44-7.21 edges; tau 19-36; corr(tau, k) -0.12. 11 trajectory labels + "other".
- **Smoke, 50 sets per truth:**
  - False pass: memory-only truth 0.02, commitment-only truth 0.02.
  - Full truth (lambda 0.935): pass 1.00, lambda recovery 1.00 (median 0.935).
  - lambda 0.85 and lambda 0.97: pass 1.00 and 1.00. Half slope: 1.00.
  - This is far stronger than on the sealed embryo set (power 0.94, lambda 0.97 0.68, half slope 0.62), as the wider k range should give.
- **Analytic check FAIL: mean max bin difference 0.0102 against the 0.01 bar** (memory truth 0.0106, l085 0.0108; under 0.01 for com, l097, half). **Gate: FAIL; stop before the fit, as pre-registered.**
- Diagnostic (synthetic only; 200 extra sets of the full truth, simulator only, no fitting): the mean simulated agreement per tau x k bin matches the closed form within 0.0007 in all 9 bins (bias about 0). The per-set SD of a bin mean is 0.004-0.007, so the maximum over 9 bins of a single set is about 0.01 by noise alone. The check, as written (per-set maximum over bins), measures Monte Carlo noise at this bin size, not a model or simulator error.
- A changed check (e.g. bias averaged over sets, or a bar scaled to the bin SE) would be an amendment chosen after seeing this number, and needs Bence's OK. No rule changed here.

### C17-S1PL-T amendment 1: analytic check as bias averaged over sets (2026-11-20; Bence: "1")
- **Changed (one check only):** the closed form vs simulation check becomes: for each tau x k tertile bin (>= 30 pairs), the mean over 200 synthetic sets of (simulated bin mean - closed-form bin mean); PASS if the largest absolute value over bins is <= 0.01 (bar unchanged). Full truth (lambda 0.935, full slope), simulator only, no fitting, on the real train structure. New stage `analytic` in c17s1pl_fit.py writes results_c17/c17s1pl_t_analytic.json; `gate` reads it in place of the per-set maximum.
- **Why:** the check as written took the per-set maximum over 9 bins, which at this bin size is about 0.01 from Monte Carlo noise alone (per-set bin SD 0.004-0.007). What the check is meant to catch is a mismatch between simulator and closed form, which is a bias averaged over sets.
- **Stated plainly:** this amendment was chosen after seeing the failed number (0.0102). The other four checks are unchanged and were all passed with margin; the per-set maximum stays reported.
- After the gate: the `fit` stage (as C17-S1T real_fit, leave-one-founder-out, rule fixed in the pre-registration) runs on Actions (sweeps/c17s1pl_t_fit.txt), train founder clades only.

### C17-S1PL-T amendment 1 result: gate PASS (2026-11-20; local, synthetic labels on the real train structure, simulator only)
- Bias averaged over 200 sets, per tau x k bin (9 bins, 765-1,105 pairs each): largest |bias| 0.00075 (bar 0.01); per-bin SE 0.0003-0.0005, so all biases are within about 2 SE of 0. The per-set maximum (as pre-registered) is 0.0098 on this new seed and 0.0102 in the smoke.
- Other checks unchanged: false pass 0.02 / 0.02, power 1.00, lambda recovery 1.00. **Gate: PASS.** Fit dispatched on Actions (sweeps/c17s1pl_t_fit.txt).

### C17-S1PL-T fit: NOT SUPPORTED by the pre-registered rule (2026-11-20; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44814968463; train founder clades only, label major_trajectory)
- **Rule:** M_full beats both reductions in 10 of 27 eligible founder clades (needed >= 18). Pooled held-out error: full 0.0689, commitment-only 0.0693, memory-only 0.0707 (full lowest, but by 0.5% over commitment-only). **Verdict: NOT SUPPORTED.** No row goes to the parameter table.
- Per clade: commitment-only beats memory-only in 17/27; full beats commitment-only in 16/27 and memory-only in 19/27. So commitment carries most of the fit and per-edge memory adds little beyond it, which is the outcome the pre-registration predicted as possible ("M_com within noise of M_full").
- lambda in the full model is stable: 0.940 on all data, leave-one-out range 0.929-0.948 (it was recovered at 1.00 in the smoke, so this is identified, but it does not earn its place in held-out error). Commitment C(tau) rises 0.24 -> 0.79 -> 0.99 at tau 19 / 26 / 36 edges.
- Fitted label noise eps 0.57 (commitment-only 0.57, memory-only 0.43): sister arms agree far less than full commitment would predict even at deep tau. So `major_trajectory` differs within committed subclades, or tau in edges from the tree root does not track commitment well. This limits what either term can be read as.
- In-sample calibration per tau x k bin: |obs - pred| <= 0.035 (largest in the deepest-tau, short-k bin); the model under-predicts at deep tau.
- Limits as pre-registered: one embryo, shared niche, a lineage-constrained tree (biases toward commitment), k in edges as a proxy for divisions.
- Practice tick-list: selftest ok; 5 starts (spread <= 0.004); analytic check passed by amendment 1 (stated as post hoc); eps fitted; calibration reported; neutral wording (filter scan clean); A/B/C sealed and unspent.
- Model lanes: Opus wrote the amendment, code and verdict; Actions ran the fit; analytic check local (synthetic only).

### C17-S1PL-T2 (time instead of edges): STOPPED at pre-flight, not identifiable (2026-11-21; Bence: "1"; local structure read only, no labels)
- Plan was: replace split depth in edges by split date, and divisions since the split by time since the split.
- Feasibility read (tree structure only, all pairs of the stratified picker, no labels): every leaf sits at 13.5 days from the root (SD 0.000; the tree is exactly ultrametric). So time since split = 13.5 - split date for every pair: corr(split date, time since split) = -1.00. Commitment by date and memory by time since split are then both functions of the split date alone, and the nested test cannot separate them. Not pre-registered, no script written.
- What stays identifiable: split date vs divisions since the split (edges): corr -0.11 (split date 10th-90th 7.7-11.6 days); tau (edges) vs date: corr 0.55. A "commitment on a clock, memory per division" variant would be separable.

### C17-S1PL-P: feasibility pretests before proposing any next step (2026-11-21; Bence: "can you just do a lot of pretest and see what could even work? before suggesting me a lot of shit that cannot??")
- Serves: C17-S1PL. No sibling agreement computed, no fit on real labels; A/B/C untouched.
- P1 clock + division variant (commitment by split date, memory per division): power and false pass on synthetic labels on the real train structure (same simulator and rule), few sets locally.
- P2 finer label: label columns in the metadata header; for each candidate column, level counts and readout gate (pairs with >= 4 non-missing per arm, clades with >= 30 pairs) on train rows only.
- P3 other trees in the source release (more embryos, a tree not built with cell types): file listing only.
- P4 which other systems in the parameter table have split depth per pair (needed for any stage-aware test): project files only.
- Pass bar for proposing a step: identifiable (|corr| < 0.8 between the two terms), power >= 0.8 and false pass <= 0.10 in the pretest, readout gate met.
- P5 added (2026-11-21): the source release also ships the same backbone dated without the literature minimum-age ladder (tree_building/results/3-dated-tree/merged_minB2h_unconstrained.nwk). Structure-only comparison of the train pairs' split dates (constrained vs unconstrained), downloaded on the runner, sha256 recorded. Pass bar for the clock variant: same topology and Spearman of split dates >= 0.9.
- **Correction to the C17-S1PL-T limits:** "lineage constrained" in the tree file name means the dating is constrained by a literature cell-count ceiling (minimum node ages), not that cell types shaped the topology (tree_building/3_date_tree/README.md: NJ backbone from edits, then LSD2 dating with a min-age ladder). So the limit "topology shaped by cell types, biases toward M_com" does not apply; the date-dependence of early splits does.
- P6 added (2026-11-21): the power pretests used the simulator's label noise eps 0.12, but the real C17-S1PL-T fit gave eps 0.57. Re-run power at eps 0.57 for the clock variant, the finer label, and the edge test already run (edges, major_trajectory), to see whether that test's NOT SUPPORTED was a real negative or underpowered. 20 sets per truth, synthetic labels only.

### C17-S1PL-P results: what can work (2026-11-21; runs https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44897589866 (P1/P2), https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44898328623 (P5), https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/44899256207 (P6); synthetic labels on the real train structure; no sibling agreement computed)
- P1 clock + division (commitment by split date, memory per division edge): identifiable (corr(date, k) -0.13). Power at eps 0.12: false pass 0.00 / 0.00, power 1.00, half slope 1.00, lambda recovery 1.00. **PASS.**
- P2 finer label `celltype`: 24 categories after pooling (vs 12), Q median 0.09 (vs 0.24); readout gate passes (8,146 pairs, 27 eligible clades). Power as P1. **PASS.**
- P3 other trees in the release: no second embryo tree. A tree "not built with cell types" is not needed: the topology never used them (correction above). **Nothing to run.**
- P4 other systems with split depth per pair: only the two embryo-tree systems (PEtracer, C17-S1T; this tree), both already tested. Blood and gastruloid systems have no trees. **FAIL: nothing to carry a stage-aware model to.**
- P5 dating: the unconstrained-dating tree has the same clades (all 8,146 train pair nodes found by leaf set); split dates Pearson 0.995, Spearman 0.995; the age ladder shifts dates by a median of 2.4 days but keeps their order. corr(date, k) -0.11 unconstrained. **PASS: the clock variant does not hinge on the ladder.**
- P6 power at the real label noise eps 0.57 (20 sets per truth): clock: false pass 0.00 / 0.05, power 1.00, half 0.95; celltype: 0.00 / 0.00, 1.00, 1.00; **edges with major_trajectory (the test already run): 0.00 / 0.00, 1.00, 1.00.** So C17-S1PL-T was powered for the planted effect even at the real noise. Its NOT SUPPORTED is a real negative for that model, not a power failure. The real data differ from the planted truth (full beats commitment-only by 0.5% pooled; calibration misses up to 0.035).
- Both passing variants would be further models on the same train data that already gave NOT SUPPORTED; any pre-registration must count them (2 more looks) and say so.

## C17-S1PL-T3: clock + division model, commitment by split date and memory per division, TRAIN founder clades only (pre-registered 2026-11-21; Bence: "and go 1")
- **Serves: C17-S1PL** (novelty lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md, finding added 2026-11-21: partly published; time vs division as the driver of differentiation timing is classic, the nested fate model on a dated embryo tree was not found). Feasibility: C17-S1PL-P (P1, P5, P6 passed).

A pass here is exploratory only; a claim would need a confirmation on sealed partition A with Bence's OK. Also reported, not tested: the held-out error of this model vs the edge model of C17-S1PL-T (which commitment clock fits better).

Power: C17-S1PL-P P1 and P6 (synthetic labels on this structure, 20 sets per truth): false pass 0.00 / 0.00 at eps 0.12 and 0.00 / 0.05 at eps 0.57; power 1.00 at both; half slope 1.00 / 0.95; lambda recovery 1.00. Gate also run inside the fit job before any real label agreement: analytic bias averaged over 200 sets (amendment 1 form) <= 0.01 on the clock covariate, else stop.

## C17-S1PL-P2: pretest of a sealed-A test "commitment follows the date clock better than edge depth" (pre-registered 2026-11-21; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C17-S1PL.** Decides whether the clock-vs-edge-depth signal of C17-S1PL-T3 (reported, not tested) can be confirmed on sealed partition A at power >= 0.8. Pretest only; no sealed read of any kind.
- **Planned A test (what is being pretested):** both full models frozen at their train full-data fits (clock: C17-S1PL-T3; edge: C17-S1PL-T), covariates standardised by train mean/sd. On A pairs, per-founder weighted held-out error of each; d_f = err_edge - err_clock per eligible A founder (>= 30 pairs). Rules evaluated: R1 one-sided paired t over founders p < 0.05 and pooled d > 0; R2 pooled d > 0 and clock lower in >= 2/3 of founders.
- **Method:** founder heterogeneity is the binding noise (train per-founder differences: mean 0.0037, sd 0.0097, 19/27 positive, t 2.0). Resample the 27 train per-founder differences (full models, leave-one-founder-out errors of C17-S1PL-T and -T3, already computed) at n founders = 10-19 (A has 19 founder clades; ~13 eligible expected from the train ratio 27/38), 20,000 draws each. Effect at observed, half (selection after seeing T: winner's curse), and zero (centred: false pass). Also n = 27 (A+B pooled) for reference only.
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: founder clade; one embryo; no treatment (H22 n/a).
  2. Readout: no new data read. A's eligible count is not computed from A; it is projected from the train ratio.
  3. Used data first: train LOO errors only (spent).
  4. Power: this entry is the power check.
  5. Exposure: none new; A/B/C untouched.
  6. Literature: lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md (2026-11-21 finding).
  7. Readout gate (H21): an A test passes only with power >= 0.8 at the half effect and false pass <= 0.05.
- **Prediction:** underpowered on A alone (expected t on A ~ 2.0 x sqrt(13/27) ~ 1.4); about 70% that no rule reaches 0.8 at the half effect.
- Limits: LOO refit errors stand in for frozen-parameter errors; train founders stand in for A founders.
- Practice: seeded; neutral wording; result entry with tick-list.
- Compute: local (spent train results, seconds), c17s1pl_pretest.py apower.

### C17-S1PL-P2 result: FAIL, a sealed-A test of clock vs edge depth is underpowered; A stays sealed and unspent (2026-11-21; local; Bence: "1")
- Train per-founder differences (edge minus clock, full models, LOO): mean 0.0037, sd 0.0097, clock lower in 19/27.
- R1 (one-sided paired t over founders): power at the observed effect 0.43 at n = 13 (A projected), 0.52 at n = 19 (every A founder eligible), 0.63 at n = 27 (A+B pooled); at half effect 0.21 / 0.25 / 0.29. False pass 0.065-0.069 (slightly above 0.05: skewed differences).
- R2 (pooled d > 0 and >= 2/3 founders): false pass 0.24-0.36. Invalid as a test.
- **Verdict: FAIL** (bar: power >= 0.8 at half effect, false pass <= 0.05). No rule reaches it even with two sealed partitions pooled. As predicted (~70%). The clock-vs-edge-depth signal stays exploratory; spending A on it would waste the partition.
- Practice: seeded (20,000 draws per cell); no sealed read; A/B/C sealed and unspent; neutral wording. Lanes: Opus wrote plan, code and verdict; run locally (seconds).

## C17-S1R-P: parameter table update with the embryo-tree result, and law-test feasibility pretest (2026-11-21; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C17-S1R** (build the general model system by system; law test only at >= 3 systems per class).
- **Table (c17s1_params.py):** added "DNA Typewriter embryo tree (train)" to the pluripotent class: commitment (C 0.48 at 9.4 days, date clock) identified; memory per division edge 0.899 (leave-one-out 0.892-0.904) NOT counted as identified, because the nested test was NOT SUPPORTED in all three powered variants (C17-S1PL-T, -T3, -T4 with P3).
- **Count gate now:** committed blood 3 (LARRY, SIS, CellTag LSK), pluripotent 3 (gastruloids, PEtracer, embryo tree), neural 1.
- **Pretest (no data read; table only):**
  1. Shared parameter: blood shares heritable_share across all 3 systems; every pluripotent parameter is identified in exactly 1 system (gastruloid rho_div, PEtracer heritable_share, embryo-tree commitment). A class comparison on one parameter has at most 3 blood vs 1 pluripotent. FAIL.
  2. Power with systems as units: even 3 vs 3, the smallest attainable permutation p is 1/C(6,3) = 0.05, so p < 0.05 is impossible; 3 vs 4 gives 0.029 at best (power at a perfect separation only). FAIL.
- **Verdict:** law test NOT feasible with the current table, although the count gate is met. Do not pre-register it. What would change this: a second pluripotent system with heritable_share (or rho_div) identified, and >= 4 systems in each compared class.

## C17-S1R-P2: pretest, can a second pluripotent system give a shared parameter for the law test? (2026-11-21; Bence: "1"; log and table only, no data read, local)
- **Serves: C17-S1R.** Candidates: (a) heritable share (B38, sister arms) on the embryo tree's train founder clades, the estimand PEtracer has; (b) memory per division on the PEtracer trees; (c) a heritable share for the gastruloids; (d) a 4th blood system (chspctrack, serial half-well sampling, needs its own train estimate).
- **Checks:**
  1. (b) is already answered: C17-S1T on the PEtracer trees was NOT SUPPORTED (memory adds <= 2% beyond commitment), so rho_div is not identified there. FAIL.
  2. Best-case power for the only shared parameter (heritable share), systems as units, one-sided permutation test on the class means. Blood values held: 0.88, 0.71, 0.66; PEtracer 0.81 lies inside the blood range. Even if every new pluripotent value were 0 (the most favourable case): 3 blood vs 2 pluripotent (PEtracer + embryo tree) p >= 0.30; 3 vs 3 (+ gastruloids) p >= 0.15; 4 vs 3 (+ chspctrack, any value) p >= 0.086. No configuration of the systems we hold or can derive reaches p < 0.05. FAIL.
  3. Data existence: the C17-S1D sweep found no new public pluripotent clone-split or clonal-memory set; watch-list items (hESC sister wells, DeepTrack, E-MTAB-17351) are not available.
- **Verdict: FAIL.** No candidate in hand can make the cross-class law test feasible; computing (a), (c) or (d) would add table rows but cannot change this. Not run.
- What would change it: at least two more public pluripotent sets with sister-arm or split designs (watch list), and values that do not overlap the blood range.
- Practice: best case computed exactly (all permutations); neutral wording; nothing sealed touched. Lanes: Opus, local, seconds.

  |---|---|---|---|

## C17-S1PL-T5: W5 fit, memory per edge early vs late splits, with a commitment-step control (pre-registered 2026-11-22; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C17-S1PL** (current FOCUS step; the W5 direction of C17-S1R-P4).
- **Identification gap found before any real agreement was read** (advisor review): early/late is defined by split date, the same covariate that drives commitment. A second lambda could win by absorbing a misfit of the logistic commitment curve near the earliest splits (the very bin that motivated W5), with no memory difference. P4's null planted a logistic curve only, so its 0.025/0.05 false pass does not cover this.
- **Models (all fitted with the P4 pretest fitter `_fit_split`/`_fit3`, 5 starts, same weights):**
  - M_one: alpha, beta (date clock), lambda, eps (4 params).
  - M_split: alpha, beta, lambda_early, lambda_late, eps (5).
  - M_cstep (control, same size as M_split): alpha, beta, lambda, delta_early (commitment offset for early splits), eps (5).
  - early = split date below the train median date (8,146 train pairs; the numeric median is written into the P5 files from structure only and asserted equal in the fit).
- **Primary rule (unchanged from P4):** M_split lower leave-one-founder-out error than M_one in >= 2/3 of the 27 eligible clades AND pooled.
- **Attribution rule:** the result is read as "memory differs early vs late" only if M_split ALSO beats M_cstep by the same 2/3-and-pooled rule. If only the primary rule passes: "an early/late term helps, not attributable to memory". Else NOT SUPPORTED.
- **Gate before the fit (C17-S1R-P5, discrimination power):** synthetic labels on the train structure, commitment planted at the T3 fit (alpha -0.018, beta 1.034), eps 0.40 and 0.57, 40 sets per truth. Truths: null (lambda 0.90), split (0.85 early / 0.95 late), cstep (lambda 0.95 everywhere, commitment step delta chosen so early pairs have the same mean expected agreement as the split truth: the hardest mimic). Gate: attribution rate >= 0.8 under split AND <= 0.05 under null and under cstep, at both noise levels. If it fails, W5 is not identifiable on these pairs and is dropped without the fit (no 4th look spent).
- **Report, not tested:** lambda_early, lambda_late with LOO ranges, full-data start spread, direction of the difference, early/late pair counts per clade, fitted eps vs 0.40/0.57 (provisional above 0.57).
- Pre-flight:
  1. Unit: founder clade (27 eligible), one embryo, no treatment.
  2. Readout: major_trajectory agreement (gate met in T).
  3. Used data first: train only. A/B/C sealed and untouched.
  4. Power: P4 (primary rule) plus P5 (attribution), below.
  5. Exposure: 4th model family on these train pairs (T, T3, T4 before). No sealed confirmation path unless a separate power pretest shows one.
  6. Literature: lit/novelty/C17-S1PL.md (memory falls with differentiation, BMC Biol 2024); a late > early difference would be in kind with it.
- **Predictions:** P5 gate passes at eps 0.40 but attribution is marginal at 0.57 (~50% the gate fails overall). If the fit runs, ~60% NOT SUPPORTED or not attributable.
- Practice: seeded; selftests (split model recovers 0.80/0.95; cstep recovers delta -0.70 and lambda 0.95; rule3 truth table); neutral wording.
- Compute: GitHub Actions, sweeps/c17s1r_p5_discrim.txt (gate), then sweeps/c17s1pl_t5_fit.txt only after the gate passes and Bence's go.
- **Amendment 1 (2026-11-22, before any P5 result; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45025487353 crashed in setup, 0 sets simulated):** the cstep truth as written (lambda 0.95 everywhere, step matched to the early mean) has no solution on this structure: with late memory 0.95, no commitment offset brings the early mean agreement down to the split truth's (brentq: no sign change). Replaced by the hardest mimic defined directly: the M_cstep fitted (same fitter) to the split truth's noise-free expected agreement, then planted. Locally on train structure (no labels): alpha 0.91, beta 1.03, lambda 0.856, delta -0.94, weighted RMSE to the split truth 0.0064 (eps 0.40) / 0.0046 (0.57). Gate bar and rules unchanged. Exposure unchanged (synthetic labels only).

### C17-S1R-P5 result (2026-11-22; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45026085769)
- **Gate: FAIL.** Rates over 40 sets per cell (results_c17/c17s1r_p5_discrim_*.json):

  | truth | eps | split beats one | split beats cstep | attributed |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | null | 0.40 | 0.025 | 0.075 | 0.00 |
  | null | 0.57 | 0.05 | 0.10 | 0.025 |
  | split 0.85/0.95 | 0.40 | 1.00 | 0.425 | **0.425** |
  | split 0.85/0.95 | 0.57 | 0.95 | 0.325 | **0.325** |
  | cstep (closest mimic) | 0.40 | **0.95** | 0.00 | 0.00 |
  | cstep (closest mimic) | 0.57 | **0.95** | 0.00 | 0.00 |

- Attribution power 0.43 / 0.33, below 0.8; false attribution stays low (<= 0.025).
- **The main finding:** a commitment step with no memory difference passes the P4 primary rule 95% of the time. The P4 power PASS was real but not specific: on these pairs, a better fit for early vs late splits cannot be credited to memory.
- **Decision (pre-registered):** W5 is not identifiable on the dated-tree train pairs and is **dropped without the fit**. No real agreement was read; the 4th look on these pairs is not spent; A/B/C sealed and untouched. The fit5 stage stays in code and refuses to run (gate file shows FAIL).
- Prediction (gate fails, ~50-60%) held.
- Lesson: when a new term is defined by the same covariate as an existing curve, power must be checked against a same-size control that bends that curve (here added only because of a pre-fit review).

## C12-S2: simulated power redo for a sealed C12 look (pre-registered 2026-11-22; Bence: "1")
- **Serves: C12-S2.** Owed since RETRO_2026-11-14b: the C12-S1 power (0.55-0.57 per partition, 0.85 A+B pooled) used `z_power` on a fixed out-of-fold SE, not H17 simulation, and is provisional. This step replaces it. No look is made here.
- **Frozen sealed test (defined before any simulation; the look itself would need its own entry and Bence's OK):**
  - Readout: presence at D20 in vivo only (>= 1 assigned cell, highest-UMI rule). D40 ex vivo is dropped: it never reached 0.8 even under the optimistic arithmetic.
  - Models: M0x = log D20 size + QC + library + barcode UMI + multi-clone fraction + majority hashtag; M1x = M0x + 5 PCs of clone-mean D20 expression. HVG set, PCA loadings, scaler and logistic coefficients are fit once on all train clones and frozen; partition clones are projected and scored.
  - Statistic: delta AUC (M1x - M0x) on the partition's clones.
  - Null: the partition's state-PC rows permuted among its clones (M0x fixed), 200 permutations; p = (1 + #null >= observed) / 201; pass if p < 0.025. This is an empirical null, so no normality or zero-centring is assumed.
  - Pooled configurations are one AUC over the pooled clones (A+B; A+B+C).
- **Simulation (train only; script `c12s2_power.py`, on Actions with the `lsc` data input):**
  1. Rebuild train covariates and the D20 in vivo readout exactly as C12-S1 amendment 2. Assert 712 train units, 101 positives, train CV delta AUC within 0.005 of 0.166 (proof that the Actions data and clone map match the local ones).
  2. Generative model: logistic M1x fit on a bootstrap of train clones each simulation (parameter uncertainty), state-PC coefficients scaled by s. s is calibrated once (on the full-train fit, large pool of 20,000 bootstrap rows) so that the oracle delta AUC (true linear predictor vs its nuisance part) equals the target effect. **Target effect = 0.5 x min(train delta, train delta net of the label-shuffle mean)** (shrink 0.5 frozen).
  3. Each simulation: pseudo-train = 712 bootstrap train rows with outcomes drawn from the generative model; refit M0x and M1x; pseudo-partition = bootstrap rows at the partition's structural clone count with fresh outcomes; frozen test as above.
  4. Configurations: A 304, B 316, C 298, A+B 620, A+B+C 918 clones (structural counts, C12-S1). 1,000 simulations each.
- **Selftests (in the script, before the power run):** s = 0 gives a false-pass rate <= 0.05 (expected about 0.025); a planted large effect (s at oracle delta 0.25) gives power >= 0.95.
- **Decision rule:** power >= 0.8 on a single partition -> a one-partition look can be proposed (C12-S3, separate entry, needs Bence). Only a pooled configuration >= 0.8 -> reported, the choice to spend two partitions in one look is Bence's and is not proposed by default (Bence: keep more sealed). Nothing >= 0.8 -> C12 stays train-only, A/B/C sealed.
- **Known optimism (caveat):** the simulation uses in-sample train PC scores; a real look projects partition clones through train PCA. Not modelled; stated in the result.
- **Exposure:** C12-S0 counts, train presence fractions, train QC/library/hashtag counts, per-partition structural unit counts. No sealed outcome or sealed expression is read.
- **Pre-flight:** (1) unit: D20 clone; (2) readout: D20 in vivo presence; (3) used data first: train only, as C12-S1; (4) power: this step; (5) exposure: as above; (6) literature: H20 reading done in C12-S1; (7) readout gate: passed in C12-S1 (101 positives).
- **Compute:** Actions run (sweeps/c12s2_power.txt with the `lsc` data input; one job, ~1 h); URL logged at dispatch.
- Practice: neutral wording; FOCUS step switched to C12-S2 (Bence: "1"); C17 left at C17-S1PL.

### C12-S2 amendment 1 (2026-11-22, after the selftest, before any power figure): residual-permutation null
- **Why:** run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45048250443 reproduced C12-S1 exactly (712 units, 101 positives, train delta 0.1661; label-shuffle mean 0.0005; target effect 0.0828) but the null selftest FAILED: false-pass rate 0.111 (bar <= 0.05) at s = 0; planted power 1.00. The script stopped before any power figure, as pre-registered. Likely cause: the state PCs are correlated with size and QC, so permuting whole PC rows breaks that link and pushes the permutation null below the observed delta even with no state effect. On synthetic data with moderate correlation the plain null gave 0.047 and the residual null 0.01 (scratchpad check, not a result).
- **Change (frozen test and simulation alike):** within the partition, the state PCs are regressed on the M0x covariates (linear, with intercept); the permutation shuffles the residual rows and adds them back to the fitted part (Freedman-Lane). Statistic, models, 200 permutations, p rule and alpha are unchanged. Output file results_c12/c12s2_power_a1.json; the failed run's file is kept as the record.
- **Selftest bar unchanged** (false pass <= 0.05, planted >= 0.95). If it fails again, no power is reported and the test design goes back to Bence.
- No sealed data read; nothing else changed.

### C12-S2 result (2026-11-22; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45050001794; results_c12/c12s2_power_a1.json): train only, no sealed read
- **Reproduction:** 712 train clones, 101 present at D20 in vivo, train CV delta AUC 0.1661 (C12-S1: 0.166); label-shuffle mean 0.0005. Target effect 0.0828 (shrink 0.5).
- **Selftests (amendment 1 null): PASS.** False pass at s = 0: 0.036 (bar <= 0.05; slightly above the nominal 0.025). Planted (oracle delta 0.25): power 1.00.
- **Simulated power of the frozen test (1,000 simulations each; mean simulated delta about 0.067):**

  | configuration | clones | power |
  |---|---|---|
  | A | 304 | 0.980 |
  | B | 316 | 0.976 |
  | C | 298 | 0.977 |
  | A+B | 620 | 1.000 |
  | A+B+C | 918 | 1.000 |

- **Verdict: a single partition is powered (H19 passes for a one-partition look).** The earlier z_power figure (0.55-0.57) is withdrawn: it used a bootstrap SE of the delta that also counted label noise the permutation test conditions on, and no full-pipeline simulation.
- **Self-challenge:** (1) suspicious? The jump from 0.56 to 0.98 is large. The null is calibrated (0.036) and the effect is already halved, so the gain is from the test design, not from a bigger effect (unverified: the permutation null's centre at s_eff was not printed). (2) Not modelled: in-sample train PC scores (a real look projects partition clones through train PCA), and a linear-logistic truth. Both make the simulation optimistic to an unknown degree; the margin over 0.8 is wide. (3) Mouse/well effects beyond hashtags are untested on train. (4) The source preprint's engraftment association overlaps in kind (H20).
- **Open size check (advisor, 2026-11-22):** the null selftest covers only s = 0 in both train and partition. The case a sealed look must guard against (pseudo-train at s_eff, partition at s = 0) is not simulated, and the permutation null's mean at s_eff is not reported. Both are owed before any look; if the null centre sits well below 0, the pass rule needs 'and delta > 0'.
- **Next (needs Bence):** the size check above, then pre-register C12-S3, one oracle look on one partition (A), with the frozen test; B and C stay sealed. Novelty: published in kind (needs Bence's 'Published but proceeding' line). No look is made without his OK.
- No sealed data read.

- **Serves: C12 CLOSED** (novelty-first candidate pretests; top 3 in order CAND-F, CAND-G, CAND-D; CAND-E is CAND-G's cortical leg).

Only the mouse-id and clone-count columns were read; the bias columns stayed masked and unread, and nothing from that sheet is copied into the repo. GSE134242 has 9 recipients with 77-3,683 barcoded clones each, and the GSE299000 series we fetched is a native atlas (no transplant recipients), so the CAND-F note's "9 recipients" was wrong and the units are unknown.

No expression, cluster or annotation file; clones are not split by partition (a per-recipient count, as C17-S0b).

- **Kill rule fixed now for P2 (only if mapped):** a design-level null passes only with a concrete coupling shown on train and structural counts alone (clone count tracks cells sampled per mapped mouse; train clones' bias varies with clone size) and a simulated false-positive rate of a 7-point Spearman at the source's alpha >= 0.20. The published correlation value is never read for the design study.
- **Exposure:** the Fig. 5f clone-count column (structural, recorded under rf2020_clone prior exposure); GEO file lists. No bias value, no sealed outcome.
- **Compute:** Actions (sweeps/candf_p1_struct.txt); URL logged at dispatch.

## CAND-F-P1b: do the source's 7 mice map to the public transplant series GSE299003 / GSE307390? (structural pretest, pre-registered 2026-11-23; Bence: "Yes, run P1b")

- **Phase B (after A, same rule, columns named in an amendment before it runs):** clones per mouse under three fixed variants: any clone; >= 2 cells; >= 2 cells and >= 1 cell in the authors' HSC label. Only the HSC membership of the cell-type column is used; no other cell-type level and no bias is computed.

Every other mouse in these series is sealed by mouse in partitions.py before any bias is computed, and is the only replication data. If fewer than 3 mice remain per arm, no replication is claimed (H22).

### CAND-I-P1 novelty check (2026-11-23; classic search): **no reanalysis found**
- Europe PMC (4 queries), three web searches and the source's citing works. The only citer is a journal preprint highlight (doi 10.1242/dev.206040). No work found retests this data set with noise measured from its technical replicates.
- Not new in general: separating drift from overdispersed measurement noise is established for lineage frequency series (doi 10.1371/journal.ppat.1012090) and barcode counts (doi 10.1371/journal.pcbi.1013946). The gap is the application to this claim. Search recall is not complete.

### CAND-I-P1 power design (pre-registered 2026-11-23; Bence: "Yes, seal CAND-I")
- **Serves: C12 CLOSED.** Script candi_power.py is simulation only and reads no germline file.
- **Test:** one excess value per fish, exact one-sided sign-flip test on the mean, alpha 0.05, with 4, 8 or 12 eligible fish (one, two or three sealed partitions).
- **Pass rule (fixed now):** power at least 0.8 at an effect of 1 between-fish SD, in one sealed partition (4 fish). If it fails, CAND-I stops here. Spending more than one partition needs Bence's decision.
- **Pre-flight:** (1) unit: fish; (2) readout: simulated only; (3) used data first: no data used; (4) power: this step; (5) exposure: as in the seal entry; (6) literature: novelty check above; (7) readout gate: replicate structure passed in P1.
- **Compute:** Actions (sweeps/candi_power.txt); URL logged with the result.
- Practice: neutral wording; no train or sealed value used to set the effect size.

### CAND-I-P1 power result (2026-11-23; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45223354941; results_cand/candi_power.json): **fails the pass rule**
- One sealed partition has 4 eligible fish. The smallest possible sign-flip p is 0.0625, so power is 0 at every effect size.
- At an effect of 1 between-fish SD, power is 0.805 with 8 fish (A+B) and 0.945 with 12 (A+B+C). The effect size is assumed, not measured.
- CAND-I stops as underpowered for one partition. No germline value was read, and train, A, B and C are all unspent. Using two partitions needs Bence's decision.

### CAND-I-T0 result (2026-11-23; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45228955248; results_cand/candi_t0_struct.json)

## CAND-I-T1: train-only test of the size and drift link (pre-registered 2026-11-23; Bence: "Yes, train look")
- **Serves: C12 CLOSED.** Script candi_train.py. Train fish only, through partitions.train_only, before read counts are parsed. A, B and C stay unread.
- **Statistic:** per fish, rank correlation of log clone size with a normalised drift score, minus its mean under a neutral null matched on mean drift. Two nulls: noise fitted on the fish's technical replicates (calibrated), and multinomial noise at the observed summed depth. The second arm is not claimed to be the source's null, because the source's full text could not be fetched.
- **Fixed before reading:** clones need mean frequency at least 0.005, fish need at least 5 clones and 6 sample indices, a fish whose matched drift hits a grid edge is excluded, and at least 6 usable fish are needed. Exact one-sided sign-flip test across fish, alpha 0.05.
- **Synthetic gate, run before the table is opened:** 200 cohorts with the real train shapes. False positive rate at most 0.10, recovery of a true link at least 0.5, and wrong R2 under a true link at most 0.10. If it fails, the table stays unread and CAND-I stops.
- **Verdicts:** R1 (calibrated p <= 0.05): the link survives on train, the published claim stands, note it and move on. R2 (multinomial p <= 0.05, calibrated not, and calibrated excess at most half): a noise lead only, resting on a non-significant result at 8 fish. R3: inconclusive, stop. The train effect size informs Bence's decision on A+B and spends nothing.
- **Assumptions:** the sample index is a time point with equal spacing. A barcode absent from a replicate counts as zero; the share of such cells is reported, because per-replicate filtering would inflate replicate noise and favour R2.
- **Pre-flight:** (1) unit: fish; (2) readout: barcode reads over sample indices, train only; (3) used data first: never analysed before; (4) power: synthetic gate above; (5) exposure: as in the seal entry, plus T0 shapes; (6) literature: novelty check above; (7) readout gate: replicate structure passed in P1.
- **Compute:** Actions (sweeps/candi_train.txt); URL logged with the result.
- Practice: neutral wording; train only; no source data copied into this repo.

### CAND-I-T1 result (2026-11-23; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45230091937; results_cand/candi_train.json): **stopped at the synthetic gate**
- False positive rate 0.12 (limit 0.10), recovery 0.585 (limit 0.5), wrong R2 under a true link 0.0 (limit 0.10), R2 under the null 0.015, over 200 synthetic cohorts per condition.
- By the pre-registered rule the table was not opened. No read count or proportion of any fish was parsed, no verdict exists, and the size and drift question is untested. Train, A, B and C are all unspent.
- The miss is small and within simulation error of the limit (0.12 of 200 cohorts), and the gate used 30 null draws where the real test uses 300. The limit was not changed after seeing this. CAND-I is failed_gate. Any rerun needs Bence's decision and a new pre-registration.

## CAND-I-T1R: single rerun of the synthetic gate at full resolution (pre-registered 2026-11-23; Bence: "2")
- **Serves: C12 CLOSED.** The T1 gate used 3 calibration and 30 null draws where the real test uses 20 and 300. This rerun uses 20 and 300, a new seed (20261124) and 200 cohorts per condition. Output goes to results_cand/candi_train_r2.json; the T1 result is kept.
- **Unchanged:** every limit (false positives at most 0.10, recovery at least 0.5, wrong R2 under a true link at most 0.10), the statistic, filters, verdict rules and train-only loading of CAND-I-T1.
- **Rule:** this is the only rerun. If the gate fails, the table stays unread and CAND-I closes as failed_gate. If it passes, the script runs the T1 test on the 8 eligible train fish and the T1 verdicts apply. A and B stay sealed either way. This is a second gate attempt, and every report must say so.
- **Pre-flight:** (1) unit: fish; (2) readout: as T1, read only if the gate passes; (3) used data first: never analysed before; (4) power: this gate; (5) exposure: as T1, plus the failed T1 gate rates (synthetic only); (6) literature: novelty check above; (7) readout gate: replicate structure passed in P1.
- **Compute:** Actions (sweeps/candi_train_r2.txt); URL logged with the result.
- Practice: neutral wording; train only; limits unchanged after the first gate; no source data copied into this repo.

### CAND-I-T1R result (2026-11-23; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45235035556; results_cand/candi_train_r2.json): **R3, inconclusive; CAND-I closes**
- **Gate (second attempt):** false positives 0.09 (limit 0.10), recovery 0.595 (limit 0.5), wrong R2 under a true link 0.0, R2 under the null 0.01. Passed, so the train table was read.
- **Test not run:** 4 of 8 train fish were usable and the rule needs 6. Fish 1, 2, 5 and 16 hit the lower edge of the drift grid (Ne 10), so the neutral null could not match their drift. No p-value exists.
- **Descriptive only, no claim:** calibrated excess in the 4 usable fish was -0.035, -0.006, 0.030 and 0.273.
- **Self-challenge:** the gate simulated Ne 300 and noise slope 1.5, while the train fish fitted Ne 100 or lower and slopes 0.48 to 0.88, so the gate did not cover the real regime. Between 7% and 52% of replicate cells per fish were zero, so replicate noise may be overestimated if the source filters per replicate. Sample spacing remains an assumption.
- **Decision:** by the fixed rule CAND-I stops as failed_gate. The grid was not widened after seeing this. Train has now been read; A, B and C remain unread and unspent.

## CAND-I-E1: exploratory wider-grid look at the train fish (pre-registered 2026-11-23; Bence: "Exploratory wider grid")
- **Serves: C12 CLOSED.** Exploratory and data-informed, because the T1R train values were seen first. It supports no claim. Script candi_explore.py reads train fish only, through candi_train.load_train. A, B and C stay unread.
- **Changes from T1R:** drift grid Ne 0.316 to 10,000 (19 points). The gate is a parametric bootstrap from each fish's own clone frequencies, fitted noise and matched Ne, at the real resolution (20 calibration, 300 null draws, 200 cohorts per condition). A second noise fit treats replicate zeros as missing.
- **Unchanged:** statistic, clone and fish filters, grid-edge exclusion, at least 6 usable fish, one-sided sign-flip test at alpha 0.05, gate limits (false positives at most 0.10, recovery at least 0.5).
- **Readings:** E1, calibrated and zero-as-missing arms both p <= 0.05: consistent with the source, note it and move on. E2, multinomial p <= 0.05, calibrated not, calibrated excess at most half, and zero-as-missing also not significant: a noise lead, and only then may Bence decide on A+B. E3, anything else or a failed gate: CAND-I stays closed, with no further variants on this set.
- **Pre-flight:** (1) unit: fish; (2) readout: barcode reads over sample indices, train only; (3) used data first: train already read in T1R, hence exploratory; (4) power: bootstrap gate above; (5) exposure: T1R train values, including which fish hit the grid edge; (6) literature: novelty check above; (7) readout gate: replicate structure passed in P1.
- **Compute:** Actions (sweeps/candi_explore.txt); URL logged with the result.
- Practice: neutral wording; train only; exploratory label on every report; no source data copied into this repo.

### CAND-I-E1 result (2026-11-23; run https://github.com/krenusz/cellware/actions/runs/45240685552; results_cand/candi_explore.json): **E3, inconclusive; CAND-I stays closed**
- **Exploratory, no claim.** All 8 train fish were usable on the wider grid (matched Ne 10 to 100, none at an edge).
- **Bootstrap gate failed:** false positives 0.04 (limit 0.10), but recovery of a true link only 0.165 (minimum 0.5). At the real clone counts and drift this test cannot reliably detect the link, so a null result here is uninformative.
- **Descriptive:** mean excess 0.083 calibrated (p 0.125), 0.037 with replicate zeros as missing (p 0.281), 0.125 multinomial (p 0.059). None reaches 0.05, and the effect is 0.45 fish SD.
- **Decision:** by the fixed rule no further variants are run on this set. A+B stay sealed: at 0.45 SD and this recovery, spending them is not justified. Train has been read; A, B and C remain unread and unspent.
